result.summary: On the arithmetic-and-statistics lens the document is largely sound and, where it uses a mean, conservative: every `weights` cell equals ne0*ne1, both LAYER weights totals are exact, and the column reconciles to the whole model to the element (48*383,221,760 + 16*372,244,480 + 2*248,320*5,120 + 2,645,504 F32 = 26,895,998,464, the gguf's exact element count); "3.80 GB" (3,803,452,480 B) and "1.125 bits/weight" (QK1_0=128, 18 B/block, gguf ratio 1.1250 exactly) both check out, and no figure mixes elements with bytes. I refit `cycles = F + T*tiles` myself from the raw 4B logs and reproduced all six published F/T pairs to the digit (398,003/80,915; 441,355/76,544; 489,581/23,036; 13,379/133,082; 27,294/85,084; 39,491/21,638), and every derived ratio built on them (12.4x, 1.88x, 59%, 12%, 3.5x, 6.2x) recomputes exactly. The mean choice does not flatter: the geometric mean is BELOW the cycle-weighted speedup in all ten node sets I tested, by 1.1% (decode 5-node) to 11.8% (prefill 10-node: 18.15x geo vs 20.57x weighted). The real damage is in the fit section: `F` is fitted from five points spanning only three distinct tile counts that straddle the 2 MB L3 (0.37/1.47 MB resident, 3.50 MB spilling), so the model is misspecified - "F stays put" is contradicted by the doc's own table (gemv F rises 2.95x), "12.4x the per-call fixed cost" is 6.20x once you normalise 4 tokens against 2, and "bigger than the kernel it feeds" is only t=2.08 (p~0.13, df=3) and does not survive. Separately, the doc's promise that "Regenerate any table with `bash sweep.sh --md`" is false for the LAYER rows - the tool never emits one - and the two wrong layer-7 cells are not reconstructible from any subset of the 12 measured counts.

findings.title: "F stays put" is contradicted by the table printed immediately above it
findings.claim_in_doc: "`T` collapses 3.5x (gemm) and 6.2x (gemv) as the kernel improves; `F` stays put, and stays an order of magnitude apart between the two paths. It is the shared activation path..."
findings.what_i_checked: Read the doc's own variant table and refit all six (variant x path) pairs from sweep-gemm/*.log and sweep-gemv/*.log. Computed the variant-to-variant change in F and the gemm/gemv F ratio at each stage.
findings.finding: F does not stay put on either path. gemv F goes 13,379 -> 27,294 -> 39,491, a 2.95x rise across the three repack variants - the doc prints these three numbers itself. gemm F goes 398,003 -> 441,355 -> 489,581, a 1.23x (+23.0%) rise. The companion clause is also weakening rather than steady: the gemm/gemv F gap is 29.7x at baseline, 16.2x at prefetch and 12.4x at d4, so it more than halves over the very table being described. A term that moves 2.95x while the kernel changes is not evidence for "F is not part of the kernel"; it is evidence the two-parameter model is absorbing kernel-dependent structure into the intercept.
findings.impact: Does not move any measured cycle count, but it is the sole justification offered for the section's central inference ("F is not part of the kernel ... It is the shared activation path"). With F rising 2.95x on gemv, the inference is unsupported by the fit alone; it rests entirely on the separate source-code argument.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with what the table shows: "T collapses 3.5x (gemm) and 6.2x (gemv); F drifts upward too (+23% gemm, 2.95x gemv), which the linear model cannot separate from kernel effects - the case that F is the shared activation path rests on the source, below, not on the fit."

findings.title: The 12.4x fixed-cost gap is not like-for-like: 4 tokens are compared against 2
findings.claim_in_doc: "But it carries **12.4x the per-call fixed cost** ... So decode gets a vector quantizer and prefill gets a scalar one. That is the whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap"
findings.what_i_checked: The doc's own table labels the two rows "gemv `d4` (2 tok)" and "gemm `d4` (4 tok)". The claimed mechanism - quantizing the ne10 x ne11 activation - is linear in token count, so I normalised both F values per token and recomputed the ratio.
findings.finding: 489,581/39,491 = 12.397, correct per call. But the gemm call quantizes 4 tokens and the gemv call 2. Per token: 489,581/4 = 122,395 vs 39,491/2 = 19,745, a ratio of 6.20x. Exactly half of the 12.4x is the token count, not the scalar-vs-vector quantizer. Per activation element the figures are 47.8 cyc/elem (gemm, 4 x 2560) vs 7.7 cyc/elem (gemv, 2 x 2560). The sentence "That is the whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap" therefore attributes 2x more to the scalar routine than the data supports. (A second, smaller caveat: if both F values also contain a token-independent per-call overhead C, the scalar penalty is larger than 6.20x on the quantizer alone - but C is never measured, so 6.20x is the defensible number.)
findings.impact: The headline penalty attributed to the scalar quantizer halves, from 12.4x to 6.2x. It does not change the conclusion that vectorising the quantizer is the best remaining prefill lever - a 6.2x per-token penalty on a term worth ~490K cycles is still the largest single item in a small prefill node - but the stated size of the prize is 2x too big.
findings.fix: Report both: "12.4x the per-call fixed cost, or 6.2x per token once the 4-vs-2 token difference is taken out; the per-token figure is the scalar-vs-vector penalty." Then say "That is the 6.2x per-token fixed-cost gap" rather than "the whole 12.4x".

findings.title: The fit spans the 2 MB L3 boundary, so a single T is misspecified and F is not identifiable
findings.claim_in_doc: "a node's cost splits cleanly into a per-call constant and a per-64-row-tile term. Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles`"
findings.what_i_checked: Computed the Q1_0 weight footprint of each of the five fit points at 1.125 bits/weight and compared it against the engine's 2 MB L3 (Setup row). Then examined the residual sign pattern of each fit.
findings.finding: The five points are not in one regime. attn_v/attn_k (16 tiles) hold 0.37 MB and attn_q (64 tiles) 1.47 MB - both L3-resident; ffn_gate/ffn_up (152 tiles) hold 3.50 MB and spill. A single per-tile constant T cannot represent both sides of that boundary. The residuals confirm it: the gemm d4 fit is +5.19% at attn_q, -4.22%/-4.23% at attn_v/attn_k and -0.46%/-0.49% at ffn_gate/ffn_up - a systematic hump, not noise, and the same sign pattern (weaker) appears in gemv d4 (+0.90 / -1.14 / -1.06 / -0.07 / -0.07). This is the mechanical reason F drifts 2.95x on gemv and 1.23x on gemm: the intercept is absorbing the regime change. Effectively there are only three distinct tile counts (16, 64, 152), two of them duplicated, so the fit has 3 nominal but ~1 effective degree of freedom.
findings.impact: Undermines the whole "F vs T" decomposition, not any cycle count. F=489,581 should be read as a fit artefact with an unknown cache component, not as a measured per-call constant. It does not change any published speedup ratio.
findings.fix: Either fit only the L3-resident points (attn_v, attn_k, attn_q) and report F from that regime alone, or measure F directly - e.g. instrument `forward_mul_mat` to bracket the quantize loop with its own cycle counter, or add a marker around repack.cpp:4456-4469 - and report a measured F instead of an inferred one. One extra ROI leg would replace the whole fit.

findings.title: The quoted goodness of fit belongs to the fit that does NOT produce the headline number
findings.claim_in_doc: "Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles` (gemv residuals within 1.1%):" - followed by a table whose headline row is the gemm one, `489,581`.
findings.what_i_checked: Computed max relative residual for all six fits from the raw logs.
findings.finding: The gemv fits are indeed tight (max relative residual: baseline 0.28%, prefetch 0.11%, d4 1.14%) - though 1.14% is marginally outside the stated "within 1.1%". The gemm fits are not, and the doc never says so: gemm baseline 0.21%, prefetch 0.91%, **gemm d4 5.19%** - 4.6x worse than the number quoted, and it is the gemm d4 fit that yields F=489,581, the figure every downstream claim in the section rests on. A concrete consequence: that fit predicts 4B attn_v at F + 16T = 858,152 cycles against a measured 823,397, an overprediction of 4.22%, so the "59% of attn_v's total" mixes a fitted numerator with a measured denominator the fit does not actually reproduce.
findings.impact: No published cycle count changes. It makes the fit look ~5x more trustworthy than it is at exactly the point where the reader is being asked to trust it. Reported against the fit's own predicted total, F is 57.1% of attn_v, not 59.5%.
findings.fix: State residuals per fit: "max relative residual 0.2-1.1% (gemv) and 0.2-5.2% (gemm); the gemm d4 fit, which yields F=489,581, is the loosest of the six." Also correct "within 1.1%" to "within 1.2%".

findings.title: "Regenerate any table with sweep.sh --md" is false for the LAYER rows - and that is how the layer-7 error got in
findings.claim_in_doc: "Regenerate any table with `MODEL=27b NODES="..." bash sweep.sh --md`." and the Reproducing section's two `--md` commands "# layer 6" / "# layer 7".
findings.what_i_checked: Read sweep.sh's md() function, then ran both published --md commands (read-only: md() only parses existing logs, it starts no simulation) and diffed the output against the doc.
findings.finding: The tool emits an **ALL n** row summing only the gate-passing, four-stage nodes - `ALL 6` = 1,415,983,905 / 199,828,560 / 186,547,213 / 66,951,649 for layer 6, and `ALL 4` = 378,118,875 / 56,300,390 / 53,185,442 / 20,258,726 for layer 7. It never emits a LAYER row, never carries a row from another node, and never prints the weights total. Both LAYER rows in the doc are therefore hand-arithmetic. Layer 6's happens to be right (ALL 6 + the two ssm rows = 1,417,870,831, exact, at every stage). Layer 7's two wrong cells are not a subset error: I brute-forced every subset of the 12 measured values at that stage, and every multiset with each node used up to twice, and nothing sums to 241,152,929 or to 225,336,152. Both are ~1.236x their true value (1.2364 and 1.2358), which looks like a scaling, not a mis-selection - so they cannot be traced to any measurement on disk. The tool also prints 15.02x for layer 7, not the doc's 17.65x.
findings.impact: A third party following the doc's instructions gets a different table shape and two different layer-7 numbers, with no way to tell which is authoritative. The two bad cells inflate layer 7's +repack and +prefetch totals by 23.6%.
findings.fix: Correct the two cells to 195,052,238 and 182,336,759, and change the promise to name what is generated and what is not: "the per-node rows regenerate with `bash sweep.sh --md`; the LAYER rows and the three carried `ffn_*` rows are added by hand." Better: teach md() to emit the LAYER row so the arithmetic cannot drift again.

findings.title: The "3.2x cheaper per token" demonstration is taken at the stage where prefill's advantage peaks
findings.claim_in_doc: "The absolute cycles show it without any ratio. On `ffn_gate` at `+repack`: ... Prefill does twice the tokens in 62% of the cycles -- 3.2x cheaper per token"
findings.what_i_checked: Computed the prefill-vs-decode per-token cost ratio for all five four-stage 27B nodes at all four build stages.
findings.finding: The arithmetic is exact (3.229x), and the doc does name the stage. But +repack is where the gap is widest, and the gap shrinks monotonically as the kernel improves: on ffn_gate the per-token ratio is 1.01x (upstream), 3.23x (+repack), 2.19x (+prefetch), 1.79x (+vd4dots). Across the five nodes: 3.04-3.23x at +repack but only 1.48-1.79x at the shipped d4 build. The same collapse appears in the fit table on the next page - per-token T ratio 3.29x at +repack, 2.22x at prefetch, 1.88x at d4 - so the doc's own two per-token figures (3.2x and 1.88x) are consistent but a reader cannot see why they differ.
findings.impact: No number is wrong. A reader carries away 3.2x as prefill's per-token advantage when the shipped configuration delivers 1.8x. It does not change any published speedup.
findings.fix: Add the endpoint: "3.2x at +repack; the advantage narrows to 1.8x by +vd4dots as the kernel stops being the bottleneck - the 1.88x per-token T ratio below is the same fact."

findings.title: "Bigger than the kernel it feeds" does not survive the fit's own uncertainty
findings.claim_in_doc: "at ~490K cycles per node it is the largest single item in a small prefill matmul -- bigger than the kernel it feeds."
findings.what_i_checked: Computed the standard errors and covariance of the gemm d4 OLS fit (n=5, df=3) and tested the linear combination F - 16T, which is exactly "fixed cost minus kernel cost at 4B attn_v's 16 tiles". Also computed leave-one-out and pairwise-slope ranges for F.
findings.finding: Point estimate F - 16T = 489,581 - 368,571 = +121,010, so the claim holds at the point estimate. Its standard error is 58,177, giving t = 2.08 on 3 df (p ~ 0.13) - not significant at 95%. F alone has a 95% CI of [325,770, 653,392] (+/-33%); its leave-one-out range is [452,912, 517,844] and its pairwise-slope range [407,238, 689,695], a 1.69x spread. Collapsing the two duplicate shapes to three distinct tile counts (df=1) widens the CI to [-859,029, 1,885,712], i.e. uninformative. The one genuinely hard bound is direct, not fitted: 4B attn_v costs 823,397 cycles in total, so F cannot exceed that.
findings.impact: The ordering claim ("bigger than the kernel it feeds") is the point estimate but is not statistically established. It does not change the practical conclusion - even at the CI's low end F is ~40% of a small node - and no measured cycle count is affected.
findings.fix: Soften to what the data licenses: "F is comparable to the kernel term on a 16-tile node (fit: 490K vs 369K, but the fit's uncertainty on F is roughly +/-30%, so the ordering is not firm) and is the single largest identifiable item in a small prefill matmul."

findings.title: The geometric mean understates the result everywhere - the mean choice is conservative, not flattering
findings.claim_in_doc: "All figures are geometric means over nodes, with `ssm_alpha`/`ssm_beta` excluded."
findings.what_i_checked: For every node set in the document I computed both the geometric mean of per-node speedups and the cycle-weighted speedup (sum of upstream cycles / sum of optimized cycles), with and without the two gate-failing nodes, and for layer 7 with and without the three carried rows.

geo mean | weighted | geo/weighted:

prefill L6, all 8 incl ssm: 9.67x | 20.60x | 0.470
prefill L7, 4 measured: 15.02x | 18.66x | 0.805
prefill L7, 7 incl carried: 17.65x | 20.91x | 0.844
prefill 5-node column: 20.67x | 21.29x | 0.971
prefill 10-node column: 18.15x | 20.57x | 0.883
decode L6, 6: 12.53x | 12.67x | 0.989

The geometric mean is below the weighted mean in all ten sets, by 1.1% to 19.5%; the largest understatement among published headlines is the 10-node prefill column (18.15x vs 20.57x, -11.8%). Excluding ssm_alpha/ssm_beta is also worth far less than it looks: on a cycle-weighted basis layer 6 falls only from 21.15x to 20.60x (-2.6%) when they are included, versus 20.60x to 9.67x on the geometric mean. findings.fix: Add one line so a reader does not have to wonder: "Geometric means are used throughout; the cycle-weighted equivalents are 1-12% higher (e.g. 20.57x against 18.15x on the 10-node set), so nothing here is inflated by the choice of mean."

findings.title: The five-node head-to-head amplifies the prefill-over-decode contrast by ~10% relative to the ten-node set
findings.claim_in_doc: "Decode has only five nodes measured at all four stages, so the head-to-head below uses **those same five on both sides** ... | **total** | **20.67x** | 12.64x |"
findings.what_i_checked: Compared the prefill/decode ratio implied by the 5-node column against the 10-node figures the doc reports in the next sentence.
findings.finding: Restricting to the five nodes raises prefill from 18.15x (10 nodes) to 20.67x, +13.9%, but decode only from 12.20x to 12.64x, +3.6%. The prefill-over-decode ratio therefore reads 20.67/12.64 = 1.64x on the five-node set versus 18.15/12.20 = 1.49x on the ten - a 10% amplification. The cause is benign and is exactly the doc's own thesis: the five nodes are all >= 5120 rows, excluding attn_v/attn_k where prefill's fixed cost hurts most. The constraint ("decode has only five nodes measured at all four stages") is real - I confirmed profiling_gemv_27b.md marks the other rows as 2-stage or inferred.
findings.impact: No number is wrong and the ten-node alternative is given in the very next sentence, so the reader can see both. Worth flagging only because the bolded 20.67x/12.64x pair is the one that will be quoted.
findings.fix: Move the ten-node totals into the same table as a second row rather than into the following sentence, so the 1.64x and 1.49x contrasts sit side by side.

findings.title: Notes says ssm_alpha+ssm_beta are 0.06% of the layer's weights; the true figure is 0.128%
findings.claim_in_doc: Notes: "They are 0.06% of the layer's weights but **2.7% of its optimized cycles**" - against the body's "They are 0.12% of the layer's weights".
findings.what_i_checked: Recomputed both, and looked for a denominator that yields 0.06%.
findings.finding: (245,760 + 245,760)/383,221,760 = 0.1282%. The body's 0.12% is right; the Notes' 0.06% is wrong by a factor of two. The likely origin is a denominator of both layers combined: 491,520/(383,221,760 + 372,244,480) = 0.0651%, which rounds to 0.07% but is the only nearby quantity. (For reference, the model-wide figure - 48 layers x 2 x 245,760 over 26,893,352,960 Q1_0 weights - is 0.0877%, which is the 0.09% profiling_gemv_27b.md quotes; that one is defensible for its wording "of the weights".) The 2.7% cycles half of the sentence is correct: 1,884,283/68,835,932 = 2.737%.
findings.impact: Halves the stated weight cost of the two dead nodes and contradicts the body 60 lines earlier. It strengthens rather than weakens the doc's argument (a smaller weight share makes the 2.7% cycle share look more disproportionate), so the error runs in the authors' favour.
findings.fix: Change "0.06%" to "0.13%" (or "0.12%" to match the body) and state the denominator: "0.13% of layer 6's weights".

findings.title: The stage columns do not multiply to the printed totals (rounding only)
findings.what_i_checked: Multiplied the printed stage figures and compared against the printed totals, then recomputed both from the unrounded logs.

findings.title: The RTL budget note disagrees with sweep.sh's own rule of thumb by 1.6x
findings.claim_in_doc: "Budget: the upstream legs are the expensive ones -- `ffn_down` at 4 tokens is 383M cycles, about 20 h of RTL."
findings.what_i_checked: sweep.sh's header comment states "A leg costs about 1 hour per 12M cycles", and calibrates it against the 4B pristine ffn_* legs ("~8 h each") - 95,939,361 cycles / 8 h = 12.0M cycles/h, self-consistent.
findings.finding: At 12M cycles/h, 382,982,019 cycles is 31.9 h, not "about 20 h" (which implies 19.1M cycles/h). The doc's own reproduce command sets TIMEOUT=259200000 ms = 72 h, well above either estimate, so the sweep as published will not time out; but a reader budgeting from the "20 h" figure and leaving the script default of 86,400,000 ms (24 h) would be at risk, and sweep.sh's header records that a 12 h timeout already killed the shorter 4B legs at 16-wide.
findings.impact: No result is affected. It is a planning figure that could cost a third party a full 32 h leg.
findings.fix: "about 30 h of RTL at the ~12M cycles/hour this engine sustains - keep TIMEOUT well above it, as the command above does."

findings.title: --selfcheck is a re-read of existing logs, not an independent re-measurement
findings.claim_in_doc: "bash sweep.sh --selfcheck     # gate: re-derive two published attn_v numbers"
findings.what_i_checked: Read run_leg() in sweep.sh and ran --selfcheck.
findings.finding: run_leg returns early ("have prefetch k=51") whenever the log already contains both an [roi] and an [andesim] line, so on a populated tree --selfcheck re-parses sweep-gemm/prefetch-k51.log and d4-k51.log and simulates nothing. It passed here (1,651,086 vs published 1,651,949, 0.052% apart; 823,397 vs 818,314, 0.62% apart; both inside the script's 1% band, rc=0). It is a genuine gate only on a tree where those two logs are absent, and the two reference values it checks against are published in opt_roadmap, not in this document.
findings.impact: None on the results. The gate is weaker than the word "gate" implies for anyone auditing an already-populated tree - which is the situation of every reader who receives this repo.
findings.fix: Note it: "--selfcheck re-runs the two legs only if their logs are missing; delete sweep-gemm/{prefetch,d4}-k51.log first to make it an actual re-measurement (about 20 min)."

result.summary: On the fairness axis the document is clean and, on one axis, conservative against itself: pristine gets the RVV-vectorized activation quantizer (`quantize_row_q8_0`, arch/riscv/quants.c:32) while all three repack builds pay the pure-scalar `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic` (repack.cpp:51) inside the same ROI, so the published prefill speedups understate the kernel by roughly F (~490K cycles at ne0=2560, ~980K at 27B's 5120) per node. The ssm_alpha/ssm_beta exclusion is defensible, mechanically defined and disclosed twice; it moves layer 6's cycle-weighted total only from 20.60x to 21.15x (+2.7%). The two real problems are framing, not measurement. First, "20.67x prefill vs 12.64x decode" is an artifact of the numerator: upstream is exactly linear in tokens (I measure geomean linearity 0.996 over 10 nodes), so S_prefill/S_decode is arithmetically identical to the optimized kernel's own M-tile advantage - against an upstream that had a 4-token gemm, prefill would score 12.20x/12.64x, i.e. exactly decode, and of the 7.04x "+repack" step only ~2.24x is the layout while ~3.16x is the gemm upstream does not have. Second, "measuring one of each covers the whole model" is false: `output.weight` [5120 x 248320] is MUL_MAT node #497, 1,271,398,400 weights (4.96% of the model's Q1_0 matmul weights, 3.32x one SSM layer), it PASSES the rows%64 gate on this model unlike the 4B LM head, and it is measured nowhere - though at 1 token in a 4-token prefill it is only 1.2% of upstream cycles, moving the whole-model MUL_MAT figure from 20.67x to 20.50x. There is no correctness gate in this document at all, and the only 27B evidence in the repo is one 3-token greedy fast-mode run of a binary (`bin-d4-fixed`, md5 750d5ee, 2026-08-05) that is none of the 48 sweep binaries; the sweep logs cannot help because the ROI marker ends the run at the measured node, so every log stops at the echoed prompt with zero generated tokens.

verified_ok.claim: The 'before' is not handicapped by the activation quantizer - the opposite is true
verified_ok.evidence: ggml-cpu.c:1347-1381 (ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat) quantizes src1 with `from_float` = type_traits_cpu[GGML_TYPE_Q8_0].from_float = quantize_row_q8_0 (ggml-cpu.c:298), which is RVV-vectorized on RISC-V gated only on __riscv_v (arch/riscv/quants.c:32,39). The repack path instead calls ggml_quantize_mat_t<1,GGML_TYPE_Q8_0> (repack.cpp:4461) -> ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic (repack.cpp:51, its own comment `// scalar`). Both sit inside the same ROI bracket. So every optimized prefill build pays a scalar quantizer that pristine does not; the published speedups are conservative by ~F per node.

findings.title: "Measuring one of each covers the whole model" is false: the LM head is node #497 and is measured nowhere
findings.claim_in_doc: "Every layer in the model is one of two kinds, so measuring one of each covers the whole model: **layer 6** is an SSM layer (48 of 64) and **layer 7** is an attention layer (16 of 64)."
findings.what_i_checked: Parsed the GGUF tensor table of models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf. Beyond the 64 blocks there are two Q1_0 tensors: output.weight and token_embd.weight, both [5120 x 248320]. output.weight is the LM head and is a MUL_MAT (graph-order node #497, from 48x8 + 16x7 + 1 = 497, which is the exact node count profiling_gemv_27b.md reports). Checked it against the dispatch gate at ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:4889: 248320 % 64 == 0 and 5120 % QK1_0(128) == 0, so it PASSES - unlike the 4B model's LM head, where 151669 % 64 == 53 (the failure the repo's own prior work recorded). Estimated its cost from the 27B decode rates in profiling_gemv_27b.md (ffn_gate 1.7468 upstream / 0.14421 d4 cycles per weight at 2 tokens), at 1 token, since llama.cpp emits logits only for the last prompt token.
findings.finding: output.weight holds 1,271,398,400 weights = 4.96% of the model's 25,621,954,560 Q1_0 matmul weights and 3.32x one SSM layer. It is neither of the two layer kinds, it is not in any table, and the document never mentions it. It does pass the repack gate on this model, so the omission is not hiding a dead spot - but the reader is told coverage is complete when the single largest tensor in the model is unmeasured, and cannot tell whether the 4B LM-head gate failure recurs here.
findings.impact: Small on the prefill headline, large on the coverage claim. At 1 token inside a 4-token prefill the LM head is ~1.11G upstream / ~91.7M d4 cycles = 1.22% / 2.06% of MUL_MAT cycles; folding it in moves the cycle-weighted whole-model MUL_MAT prefill speedup from 20.67x (layers only) to 20.50x. On decode it would be ~5% of the pass, five times larger.
findings.fix: Add one row: `output` 5120 x 248320, 1,271,398,400 weights, and state that 248320 % 64 == 0 so it passes the gate (explicitly contrasting the 4B LM head's 151669 % 64 == 53). Measuring it costs one leg per variant at ROI_K=497; if that is too slow, say the cycles are extrapolated and give the 1.22%/2.06% shares.

findings.title: Per-node ROI speedups are presented with no statement of what fraction of a prefill pass MUL_MAT actually is
findings.claim_in_doc: "| **total** | **20.67x** | 12.64x |" under the heading "Where the prefill speedup comes from", plus "Over prefill's full set of 10 optimizable nodes the totals are 6.62x / 1.06x / 2.58x = **18.15x**" and the bolded **LAYER** rows summing whole layers.
findings.what_i_checked: Searched the whole repo for any whole-pass or whole-layer cycle measurement. There is none: every one of the 48 logs brackets exactly one MUL_MAT (ggml-cpu.c:1744-1790 opens the ROI at node #K and ggml-cpu.c:1790/1913 closes it at node #K, since ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N defaults to 1 at ggml-cpu.c:39-40 and build.sh never overrides it). No node in the repo measures rms_norm, rope, conv1d, the gated-delta-net recurrence, flash-attn, SiLU, or the KV copies. Built the Amdahl sensitivity from the corrected layer totals: 48 x layer 6 + 16 x layer 7 + the LM head = 90,147,464,608 upstream vs 4,360,522,544 d4 for a 4-token prefill, S_mm = 20.50x.
findings.finding: The document is honest in its title ("cycles per MUL_MAT node") and never writes "end-to-end", but it also never tells the reader that MUL_MAT is not the whole pass, and the LAYER rows plus the "covers the whole model" sentence invite exactly that reading. Because S_mm is so large, the end-to-end number is extremely sensitive to a quantity nobody has measured: if non-MUL_MAT work is 0.7% of the upstream pass end-to-end falls to 18x, at 1.9% to 15x, at 3.6% to 12x, at 5.4% to 10x, at 10% to 6.95x. A rough MAC-count bound suggests the gated-delta-net recurrence alone is ~3.1M MACs per SSM layer at 4 tokens, which at 1 MAC/cycle scalar would be ~4.6% of the optimized layer (though only ~0.22% of the upstream layer) - i.e. plausibly in the range that matters. This is unresolved with the evidence on disk.
findings.impact: Caps the honest whole-model prefill claim at 20.50x from above and, on any plausible non-MUL_MAT share, well below it. It is the difference between "20.67x" and a number that could be half that.
findings.fix: One affordable measurement settles it: rebuild the d4 variant with -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N=8 and ROI_K=48 so the ROI spans all of layer 6 (~69M measured MUL_MAT cycles plus everything between them, ~6 h of RTL). The excess over the 68,835,932 sum of the eight nodes is the non-MUL_MAT share directly. Until then, add one sentence: "These are per-node kernel speedups. The MUL_MAT share of a full prefill pass is not measured here, so no end-to-end number follows from them."

findings.title: "20.67x prefill vs 12.64x decode" measures upstream's missing prefill kernel, not the optimization; "prefill takes its win from the layout" is half the story
findings.claim_in_doc: "This reproduces the 4B prefill result (6.11x / 1.04x / 2.46x) on a model 6.5x larger with a different architecture. Prefill takes its win from the **layout**; decode takes its win from **prefetch and the dot instruction**." and the 7.04x "upstream to +repack" cell.
findings.what_i_checked: The doc's own Note establishes upstream has .nrows = 1 and is exactly linear in tokens; I confirmed that (geomean gemm4/gemv2 = 1.992 over all 12 nodes, range 1.97-2.01). Under exact linearity, S_prefill / S_decode = (U4/D4_4) / (U2/D4_2) = 2*D4_2/D4_4, which is by definition the optimized kernel's own per-token M-tile advantage. Computed both sides per node from the two docs' cells: the ratio and the M-tile advantage agree to within 0.02 on every one of the 10 nodes (e.g. ffn_gate ratio 1.78 vs M-tile 1.79; attn_v ratio 1.01 vs M-tile 1.02). Also measured the M-tile advantage at the +repack stage alone: 2*gemv_repack/gemm_repack = 3.09, 3.04, 3.23, 3.23, 3.21 across the doc's five nodes, geomean 3.16, versus 7.04/2.24 = 3.14.
findings.finding: The entire prefill-over-decode advantage is the optimized kernel's M-tile sharing against a baseline that has no prefill kernel at all. Against a hypothetical upstream that had a 4-token gemm with equal tile sharing, the prefill speedup collapses to exactly the decode figure: 12.20x over the 10 nodes, 12.64x over the doc's five. And the 7.04x "+repack" step attributed to "the layout" factors as ~2.24x layout (which is precisely decode's own repack step, measured at fixed token count) times ~3.16x for introducing the 4-token gemm. The larger factor is the one the sentence does not name.
findings.impact: Does not change any measured cycle count. It changes what 20.67x means: roughly 12.6x of it is the optimization and roughly 1.6x is upstream's lack of a prefill kernel. A reader comparing this work against a competitor that already has an M-tiled prefill kernel would be misled by the 20.67x/12.64x contrast.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "Prefill's extra 1.6x over decode is the M-tile sharing upstream lacks entirely (.nrows = 1); of the 7.04x +repack step, 2.24x is the 64x1 layout - decode's own figure - and 3.16x is having a 4-token gemm at all. Against an M-tiled upstream, prefill would score the same ~12.6x as decode."

findings.title: No correctness gate anywhere in the document, and the 27B d4 build was never checked with the binaries that produced these numbers
findings.claim_in_doc: The document contains no sentence about correctness, verification, bit-exactness, output equality or accuracy. Grepping for correct/verify/identical/bit-exact/perplexity/test returns only two hits, both about ssm_alpha/ssm_beta running "the identical stock kernel".
findings.what_i_checked: (a) Read all 48 logs end to end. The ROI marker terminates the run at the measured node, so every log's last three lines are the echoed prompt "The capital of France", the [roi] line, and the cycle count - zero generated tokens. There is no free output diff to be had. (b) sweep.sh never passes --temp, so the runs sample at temp = 1.000 with a fresh random seed per leg (pristine-k57 seed 2155033143, d4-k57 seed 154147864) - even had they generated text it would not be comparable. (c) verify.sh does support MODEL=27b, but no 27B verify log exists in the repo. (d) The only 27B correctness artifact anywhere is ~/tmp/8b-runs/27b-fast-fixed-nommap.log: one andesim fast-mode run of /home/nick/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4-fixed (md5 750d5eee..., built 2026-08-05), temp 0.000, n_predict 4, 3 eval runs, producing "The capital of France is Paris." - compared by eye against an x86 host reference, not by script against a pristine rv64 run, and the run ended in a trap (mcause 0x2). That binary is none of the 48 sweep binaries (bin-d4 is md5 386ed57..., 2026-08-19; bin-d4-k48..k59 are 2026-08-24). (e) verify.sh's own header states d4 prefill is NOT bit-exact by construction: q1_gemm_64_vd4dot_vl1024 folds dx*ad[m] per q8 group and accumulates into sumf 4x per block instead of building facc once, so "PREFILL floats differ at the ULP level by construction".
findings.finding: The gate on the 27B prefill numbers is: one greedy 3-token generation, from an older binary, on the path the project itself declares is not bit-exact. The strong gates that do exist (test-repack-q1_0 13/13, check-prefetch.sh, check-vd4dots.sh) are all 4B/build-tree gates, and the numerical one (Level 1) tests the layout, not this model. No 27B pristine-vs-d4 script comparison has ever been run.
findings.impact: Does not change a cycle count, but a 20.67x with no correctness gate on the measured configuration is not yet a result. If the d4 gemm's different rounding order degrades 27B prefill quality, nothing in this evidence chain would catch it - and the summit abstract already promotes the 27B number as "with bit-identical output".
findings.fix: Run `MODEL=27b bash verify.sh` (fast mode, minutes per binary, no RTL) and paste its three PASS lines into the document, and state that only greedy text equality is claimed for d4 prefill, not bit-exactness. Raise NGEN above 16 so the check is not 3 tokens. Add a one-line Correctness section naming which build was checked and which was measured.

findings.title: The published LAYER rows are not what sweep.sh --md prints, so the stated regeneration command does not regenerate them
findings.claim_in_doc: "Regenerate any table with `MODEL=27b NODES="..." bash sweep.sh --md`." and the tables' bolded `**LAYER**` rows.
findings.what_i_checked: Ran `MODEL=27b NODES="48 49 50 51 52 53 54 55" bash sweep.sh --md`. The tool emits a row labelled `**ALL 6**` holding 1,415,983,905 / 199,828,560 / 186,547,213 / 66,951,649 - the sum over only the six gate-passing nodes - and its inline comment explicitly refuses to print a ratio there ("sum(upstream)/sum(vd4dots) is a cycle-weighted aggregate ... which reads like a per-node speedup without being one"). The document's row is labelled `**LAYER**` and holds 1,417,870,831 / 201,715,460 / 188,434,482 / 68,835,932, the sum over all eight nodes including ssm_alpha and ssm_beta.

That is defensible as a physical layer total, but it breaks the guarantee the document offers, and it is exactly the kind of hand-editing that produced the layer-7 LAYER row's +23.6% error the lead auditor found in the +repack and +prefetch cells.
findings.impact: No per-node figure changes. It means the document and the tool cannot be diffed automatically, which is the stated defence against drift, and it explains how a wrong row survived.
findings.fix: Either teach sweep.sh --md to emit both an ALL-nodes and an optimizable-only sum row (and generate the doc's row from it), or annotate the LAYER row as hand-summed over all N nodes including the gate failures, and re-derive its cells from the table above it.

findings.title: "Vectorizing it is the clearest remaining prefill win" - the vector twin the doc points to does not exist in the tree
findings.claim_in_doc: "Its vector twin is gated behind `__riscv_zvfh`, and the measurement build sets `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`." ... "That is the whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap ... Vectorizing it is the clearest remaining prefill win."
findings.what_i_checked: repack.cpp:344-352 reads `#if defined(__riscv_zvfh) && defined(__riscv_v) ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1(...) #else ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic(...)`. Grepped the entire ggml/ and tests/ trees for `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1` excluding the _generic name: two hits only, the declaration at repack.h:208 and this one call site. There is no definition anywhere - no arch/riscv implementation, no other backend.
findings.finding: The wording implies a working vector quantizer exists and is merely switched off by the measurement build's -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF. It does not; the symbol is declared and called but never defined, so building with ZVFH on would fail to link. Separately, "that is the whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap" is a causal claim resting on two fitted intercepts plus a source reading; no experiment isolates the quantizer (no ZVFH=ON build, no counter, no A/B).
findings.impact: No measured number changes. It misrepresents the size of the follow-up work - a kernel to write, not a flag to flip - and overstates the certainty of the attribution.
findings.fix: Say "the vector path is a stub: ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1 is declared (repack.h:208) and called under __riscv_zvfh (repack.cpp:348) but not implemented, so a vector quantizer has to be written, not enabled." Soften "the whole" to "the mechanism that accounts for it" until an A/B isolates it.

findings.title: The F+T*tiles fit's quality is quoted for the gemv, but the argument is about the gemm, whose fit is 4.7x worse
findings.claim_in_doc: "Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles` (gemv residuals within 1.1%)" followed by "`F` is 59% of 4B `attn_v`'s total" and "it carries **12.4x** the per-call fixed cost".
findings.what_i_checked: Refit both paths from sweep-gemm/ and sweep-gemv/ over the five ne0=2560 nodes. Reproduced every published coefficient exactly. Max residuals: gemv d4 1.14% (attn_v), gemm d4 5.19%. Per-node gemm d4 residuals are attn_q +5.19%, attn_v -4.22%, attn_k -4.23%, ffn_gate -0.46%, ffn_up -0.49% - a systematic curve, not noise, and it is largest precisely on attn_v/attn_k, the nodes the fit is invoked to explain. Solving F exactly from attn_v and ffn_gate instead gives F = 452,901 (not 489,581), i.e. 55% of attn_v rather than 59.5%.
findings.finding: The parenthetical reports the better of the two fits and omits the worse one, in a section whose entire subject is the gemm's F. The gemm is not affine in tiles to the precision the quoted figures imply.
findings.impact: The conclusion survives - F is still the largest single item in a small prefill matmul and still an order of magnitude above the gemv's - but 489,581, "59%" and "12.4x" carry roughly +/-8% model uncertainty, not three significant figures. No headline speedup is affected.
findings.fix: Write "(gemv residuals within 1.1%, gemm within 5.2%)" and round to "F is roughly half a million cycles, about 55-60% of 4B attn_v's total" and "an order of magnitude above the gemv's".

findings.title: ssm_alpha/ssm_beta exclusion: defensible and disclosed, but it inflates even the cycle-weighted layer figure by 2.7% and the caption does not say which rows the 20.60x covers
findings.claim_in_doc: "Geometric mean over the layer's 6 optimizable nodes: **20.60x**. `ssm_alpha` and `ssm_beta` are excluded from every average in this document, for the reason given directly below."
findings.what_i_checked: Computed layer 6 both ways from the doc's own cells. All 8 nodes: 1,417,870,831 / 68,835,932 = 20.598x cycle-weighted. The 6 optimizable nodes only: 1,415,983,905 / 66,951,649 = 21.149x. Per stage, with ssm 7.029 / 1.070 / 2.737; without 7.086 / 1.071 / 2.786. ssm share: 0.128% of layer-6 weights, 0.133% of its upstream cycles, 2.74% of its d4 cycles. Verified the exclusion rule is mechanical and matches the dispatch gate exactly (sweep.sh's md() uses `skip = (d[2] % 64 != 0)`, the same test as repack.cpp:4889), not a hand-kept name list.
findings.finding: The case for the exclusion is strong: no build touches these tensors, all four cycle counts agree to 0.3-0.5%, they measure a different kernel, and a geometric mean is brutal to values at 1.00 (the tool's own comment: two of them drag a 20x layer to 9.7x). The case against is that the exclusion is not cost-free - the honest cycle-weighted layer total is 20.60x and the excluded-node figure is 21.15x, so dropping them buys 2.7% - and that the LAYER row includes them while the geomean directly above the caption does not, which a skimming reader cannot see.
findings.impact: +2.68% on the layer-6 cycle-weighted total; the geometric-mean framing itself is unaffected. Changes no conclusion.
findings.fix: Add the counterpart number in one clause: "Cycle-weighted over all eight nodes the layer is 20.60x; over the six the kernel is applied to, 21.15x." And label the geomean row explicitly "6 of 8 nodes".

findings.title: The layer-7 rows carried from layer 6 are justified with the tighter of the two agreement measurements the document itself reports
findings.claim_in_doc: "The carry is sound: `ffn_gate` and `ffn_up` are themselves the same shape and were measured **0.11%** apart at upstream and **0.01%** apart at `d4`."
findings.what_i_checked: Both figures reproduce (0.106% and 0.014%). But ffn_gate and ffn_up are adjacent nodes in the same layer at the same graph position, so their agreement is the run-to-run floor, not evidence about a different graph position. The relevant same-shape-different-position pair is in this document's own Notes: "`ssm_out` and `attn_output` are the same shape (6144 x 5120) and agree to 2.4% at upstream" - I confirmed 2.39% - and profiling_gemv_27b.md says of exactly this, "K=60/61/62 are inferred on that basis, so their upstream column carries roughly 2.6% uncertainty".
findings.finding: The looser, more applicable 2.4% bound is present in the document but is not the one cited to license the carry, and unlike the sibling document this one attaches no uncertainty to the carried upstream cells.
findings.impact: About 2.4% on the upstream cells of layer 7's three carried rows, which moves the 7-node geomean by roughly 1%. It does not change the ordering of any conclusion.
findings.fix: Cite the ssm_out/attn_output pair instead: "identical shapes at different graph positions agree to 2.4% at upstream and 0.04% at d4, so the carried upstream cells carry ~2.4% uncertainty and the d4 cells effectively none."

findings.title: The layer-7 table lacks the `source` column its sibling document uses, so carried rows look measured
findings.claim_in_doc: The layer-7 table's last column is `total`; rows for `ffn_gate`, `ffn_up`, `ffn_down` are formatted identically to the four measured rows. The carry is disclosed only in prose two lines below the table.
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemv_27b.md's equivalent table has a trailing `source` column reading "4 stages", "2 stages", or "inferred, = K53" on every row. profiling_gemm_27b.md has no such column, in either table.
findings.finding: Three of layer 7's seven rows - and the three highest speedups in the table, 21.57x / 21.60x / 22.44x - are visually indistinguishable from measurements. They are also the rows that lift layer 7's geomean from 15.02x (the four measured nodes, which sweep.sh --md prints directly) to the published 17.65x.
findings.impact: The 17.65x headline is 4 measured + 3 carried; the measured-only figure is 15.02x, 15% lower. The document's own tooling reports 15.02x when asked for layer 7.
findings.fix: Add the same `source` column and, next to 17.65x, state "(15.02x over the four measured nodes alone)".

findings.title: check-vd4dots.sh cannot be run against the binaries that produced the 27B numbers
findings.claim_in_doc: The Setup table's `d4` row: "+ `GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` | + `nds.vd4dots.vv`", with the codegen gates offered elsewhere in the project as the proof the instruction really ran.
findings.what_i_checked: check-vd4dots.sh contains `case "$CC_CMD" in *-DQ1_VD4DOT=1*) ;; *) echo "$BUILD is not a Q1_VD4DOT build"; exit 1 ;; esac`. b-d4-k57/compile_commands.json (and every b-d4-k48..k59, all built 2026-08-24) carries `-DQ1_D4=1`, the pre-rename name; commit f480bccff renamed Q1_D4 -> Q1_VD4DOT on 2026-08-27, after the builds. The gate therefore exits 1 on the archived trees. I confirmed by reading `git show f480bccff` that the rename is behaviour-neutral (comments, macro name, two static function names, call sites), so the measurement itself is not contaminated - only the gate is inapplicable.
findings.finding: A third party cannot apply the project's own "did the instruction actually execute" gate to the exact build trees behind these 48 numbers. Running it against b-d4 (the K=51 tree) recompiles from HEAD, whose compile_commands.json was regenerated 2026-08-27 14:49 while bin-d4 dates from 2026-08-19 - so it checks HEAD's codegen, not the measured binary's.
findings.impact: No number changes. It blocks the cheapest independent confirmation that the d4 legs really ran on nds.vd4dots rather than falling back to the generic C path - a failure mode check-vd4dots.sh exists precisely because it happened before ("gemm ran generic for the whole F8 sweep").
findings.fix: Widen the guard to `*-DQ1_VD4DOT=1*|*-DQ1_D4=1*` so the archived trees are accepted, and note in the Reproducing section that the 27B trees predate the rename.

findings.title: The same quantity is reported with different denominators across the two documents, with no note
findings.claim_in_doc: This doc: "They are 0.12% of the layer's weights" (body) and "They are 0.06% of the layer's weights" (Notes). Sibling doc: "They are the only two gate failures in the model: 0.09% of the weights but 1.7% of the optimized cycles."
findings.what_i_checked: 2 x 245,760 / 383,221,760 = 0.128% (per SSM layer) - so the body's 0.12% is right and the Notes' 0.06% is wrong by 2x, as the lead auditor established. The sibling's 0.09% is a different denominator: 48 x 491,520 / 25,621,954,560 (all model matmul weights) = 0.092%. Its "1.7% of the optimized cycles" is per layer 6 of decode: 948,863 / 56,958,424 = 1.67%; this doc's 2.7% is per layer 6 of prefill: 1,884,283 / 68,835,932 = 2.74%.
findings.finding: Three different percentages (0.12, 0.09, 0.06) for one fact, two of them correct under different denominators and one simply wrong. Similarly the decode stage figures differ between docs by rounding: this doc's 2.24x x 1.60x = 3.584 versus the sibling's 3.57x for the same step.
findings.impact: None on any speedup. It costs a careful reader time and makes the pair look less carefully joined than it is.
findings.fix: Fix the Notes to 0.13%, and state the denominator inline in both docs ("0.13% of an SSM layer's weights; 0.09% of the model's").

result.summary: On the harness-fairness question the verdict is: the A/B is not rigged, and where it is unfair it is unfair AGAINST the optimization. All 48 legs bracket the identical tensor at nrows=4, no measurement binary carries the ANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF knob, GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF removes nothing for a Q1_0 tensor except the Q1_0 repack itself (llamafile sgemm has no Q1_0 case and is ON in both arms per the logs' own system_info line), and every d4 binary really executes nds.vd4dots.vv (32 custom-2 instructions in each of q1_gemv_64d4_vl1024 and q1_gemm_64d4_vl1024, zero in the other three) rather than silently falling back. sweep-gemm-27b.out shows all 48 legs as fresh "run" in one pass with zero resumes and zero non-zero exits; the only re-run anywhere (sweep-gemm-retry.out) is the two 4B *pristine* legs that timed out, i.e. the re-run helped the "before". The two real fairness problems are asymmetries the document does not put in front of the reader: (1) pristine quantizes activations with the RVV `quantize_row_q8_0` while the repack builds use the scalar `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1` (~490K cycles/node at ne0=2560, 6%-60% of each published d4 number) - removing that asymmetry raises the 10-node geomean from 18.15x to 23.3-24.5x and attn_v/attn_k from 11.40x to 24-29x, dissolving the doc's "speedup tracks node size" story; and (2) the one-time repack, which runs at model load outside the ROI, costs 58-141x one measured d4 matmul of the same tensor and inflates 27B model load from 162.1 s to 460-505 s in the logs' own timestamps, yet is never mentioned. Separately, the doc's stated cause for the scalar quantizer ("its vector twin is gated behind __riscv_zvfh") is factually wrong: no vector twin exists anywhere in the tree.

verified_ok.claim: Every one of the 48 legs brackets the same tensor, shape and nrows as its three A/B partners - no leg measures a different node.
verified_ok.evidence: For each K in 48..59 I extracted the `[roi] MUL_MAT` line from all four /home/nick/work/llama.cpp/sweep-gemm-27b/{pristine,baseline,prefetch,d4}-k$K.log and sorted -u: exactly 1 distinct string per K (e.g. k=57 -> `blk.7.attn_v.weight [5120 x 1024] nrows=4` in all four). All 48 logs contain the identical prompt echo `The capital of France[roi]`.

verified_ok.claim: The ANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF experiment knob is not compiled into any measurement binary.
verified_ok.evidence: `strings -a bin-{pristine,baseline,prefetch,d4} | grep -c mcache_ctl` = 0 for all four, while `grep -c 'roi] MUL_MAT'` = 1. The knob's fprintf at ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:1751-1762 would leave the string `[roi] mcache_ctl 0x%llx -> 0x%llx` in .rodata; build.sh only passes -DANDESIM_ROI_CLEAR_DPREF for the `prefetch-nodpref`/`baseline-nodpref` targets, which the sweep never uses.

verified_ok.claim: The d4 leg genuinely runs nds.vd4dots.vv; it is not a silent fallback to the generic C kernel.
verified_ok.evidence: Histogram-diffing the custom-2 (`.insn 4, 0x...5b`) encodings between bin-prefetch and bin-d4 isolates 13 encodings of the form 0x13xxxx5b present only in d4. Attributing them per function in bin-d4-k57 gives 32 in `q1_gemv_64d4_vl1024` and 32 in `q1_gemm_64d4_vl1024`; bin-prefetch-k57 / bin-baseline-k57 / bin-pristine-k57 have zero in those kernels. Counts are identical (75 total, 64 in-kernel) across bin-d4, bin-d4-k48, -k55, -k57, -k59. This matters because check-vd4dots.sh's own header records `(This was real: gemm ran generic for the whole F8 sweep.)`

verified_ok.claim: No leg was re-run until it looked good. The resume rule structurally cannot re-run a leg that already produced a number.
verified_ok.evidence: sweep.sh run_leg: `if [ -f "$log" ] && grep -q '^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" && grep -q '\[roi\] MUL_MAT' "$log"; then echo "have ..."; return 0; fi` - a complete log is skipped, only an empty/truncated/timed-out one is re-run. sweep-gemm-27b.out contains 48 `run` lines, 0 `have` lines, 0 `exit N` lines: the whole 27B grid is one clean pass.

verified_ok.claim: The only re-run in the evidence set favoured the 'before', not the 'after'.
verified_ok.evidence: sweep-gemm.out (4B) ends with `pristine k=56: exit 1` and `pristine k=55: exit 1` and both cells show PENDING in its table; sweep-gemm-retry.out re-runs exactly those two pristine legs (82,690,333 and 95,939,361 cycles). The two legs that failed and were retried are upstream legs - the expensive side. sweep.sh's own comment explains the cause: `12 h was NOT enough: the two largest upstream prefill legs ... timed out at 12 h when the grid was running 16-wide`.

verified_ok.claim: GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF removes nothing that upstream would have applied to a Q1_0 matmul other than the Q1_0 repack itself.
verified_ok.evidence: ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt:590-592 makes GGML_CPU_REPACK define GGML_USE_CPU_REPACK; the define has exactly two uses (ggml-cpu.cpp:64 registers the CPU_REPACK extra buffer type, ggml-cpu.cpp:628 adds the feature string). ggml_repack_get_optimal_repack_type dispatches on `cur->type`, and for GGML_TYPE_Q1_0 (repack.cpp:4884-4892) the only candidate is `q1_0_64x1_q8_0`. Turning it off therefore cannot cost a Q1_0 tensor a q4_0/q4_K/q6_K/iq4_nl/mxfp4 kernel it never qualified for.

verified_ok.claim: llamafile sgemm is enabled in BOTH arms and is inert for Q1_0, so it is not a hidden pristine handicap.
verified_ok.evidence: Every log's system_info line reads `LLAMAFILE = 1` (pristine) and `LLAMAFILE = 1 | REPACK = 1` (the other three). ggml/src/ggml-cpu/llamafile/sgemm.cpp has cases only for F32, BF16, F16, Q8_0, Q4_0, Q5_0, IQ4_NL - no GGML_TYPE_Q1_0 - so llamafile_sgemm returns false and pristine falls through to the normal vec_dot path in both worlds.

verified_ok.claim: `RVV_VLEN = 128` in the logs is not a contradiction of the Setup table's 'VLEN 1024'.
verified_ok.evidence: ggml-cpu.c:768 sets `ggml_riscv_arch_features.rvv_vlen = __riscv_vlenb()`, i.e. VLEN in BYTES. 128 bytes = 1024 bits, which also satisfies the repack gate `__riscv_vlenb() * 8 >= 512` at repack.cpp:4889.

verified_ok.claim: The document's published F/T fixed-cost table is exactly reproducible from the raw 4B logs.
verified_ok.evidence: Independent least-squares of cycles = F + T*(rows/64) over the five ne0=2560 4B layer-7 nodes reproduces all six published values to the digit: gemm baseline F=398,003 T=80,915; prefetch 441,355 / 76,544; d4 489,581 / 23,036; gemv baseline 13,379 / 133,082; prefetch 27,294 / 85,084; d4 39,491 / 21,638. The derived claims check too: 489,581/39,491 = 12.40x ('12.4x the per-call fixed cost'), 10,819/5,759 = 1.879x ('1.88x more efficient per token'), 489,581/823,397 = 59.5% ('59% of 4B attn_v's total'), 489,581/3,972,668 = 12.3% ('only 12% of its ffn_gate').

verified_ok.claim: 'Upstream is exactly linear in tokens ... 1.97x to 2.01x for 2x the tokens' holds on all 12 nodes.
verified_ok.evidence: 27B gemm pristine (from sweep-gemm-27b logs) divided by 27B gemv upstream (profiling_gemv_27b.md's table) over all 12 nodes gives 1.972 (ssm_out) to 2.012 (ffn_down); every value rounds into [1.97, 2.01]. The mechanism claim also checks: ggml-cpu.c:257 is `.nrows = 1` inside the `[GGML_TYPE_Q1_0]` entry (lines 253-258).

verified_ok.claim: The doc reports geometric means over nodes and refuses the cycle-weighted sum ratio, which is the honest choice.
verified_ok.evidence: sweep.sh md()'s awk END block prints the per-stage cycle sums with an explicit comment `Summed cycles per stage, but NO ratio: sum(upstream)/sum(vd4dots) is a cycle-weighted aggregate, which the big nodes dominate and which reads like a per-node speedup without being one.` The document publishes 20.60x / 17.65x / 20.67x / 18.15x as geomeans and never divides the LAYER row.

verified_ok.claim: The tool regenerates the layer-7 table from logs alone, and the ALL-4 sums it produces are self-consistent.
verified_ok.evidence: `MODEL=27b NODES="56 57 58 59" bash sweep.sh --md` (read-only: the `--md` case is dispatched before the grid loop, and md() only cats logs via read_leg) prints the four attn rows byte-identical to the doc plus `ALL 4 = 378,118,875 / 56,300,390 / 53,185,442 / 20,258,726` and `total 15.02x`.

verified_ok.claim: The kernel commit made after the binaries were built is a pure rename, so the binaries still correspond to HEAD's behaviour.
verified_ok.evidence: f480bccff (2026-08-27) postdates the 19 Aug / 24 Aug binary timestamps, but its diff only renames Q1_D4 -> Q1_VD4DOT and the two static kernel functions; the CMake switch `-DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` is unchanged in build.sh. The stale names are visible in the shipped binaries (`q1_gemv_64d4_vl1024`), confirming the provenance without implying a behavioural difference.

verified_ok.claim: The one-time repack hook is upstream code, not something this branch introduced to shift cost out of the ROI.
verified_ok.evidence: `git log -L` on `ggml_backend_cpu_repack_buffer_set_tensor` in ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp returns a single commit, f470bc36b `ggml-cpu : split arch-specific implementations (#13892)` by axunlei@gmail.com - upstream. The same hook drives the q4_0_4x4/8x8, q4_K, q5_K, q6_K, iq4_nl, mxfp4 and q8_0 repacks.

verified_ok.claim: The gemm M-tile citation `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1967-1972` is accurate.
verified_ok.evidence: Lines 1958-1972 set up four activation pointers a0..a3 into the same 4-token tile and feed them to `q1_vd4dots_4acc_m2(&acc0,&acc1,&acc2,&acc3, w, a0[c/4], a1[c/4], a2[c/4], a3[c/4])` against one weight vector `w`, with the in-source comment `the 4 output rows already share one weight vector`.

findings.title: The A/B does not run the same activation quantizer: pristine gets the RVV one, the repack builds get a scalar one with a libm call per element
findings.claim_in_doc: "`forward_mul_mat` quantizes activations before the kernel runs (`repack.cpp:4456-4469`) ... **4 tokens** ... take `ggml_quantize_mat_t<1, GGML_TYPE_Q8_0>` ... a **pure scalar** loop ... So decode gets a vector quantizer and prefill gets a scalar one." and "**Total speedup tracks node size.** `attn_v`/`attn_k` (1024 rows) reach 11.40x while everything from 5120 rows up reaches 18.9-22.4x."
findings.what_i_checked: Traced both arms from source to binary. Repack arm: repack.cpp:4459-4462 calls ggml_quantize_mat_t<1, GGML_TYPE_Q8_0> for i11 in [0, ne11-ne11%4) - with ne11=4 that is one call covering all four rows - which lands on the scalar routine defined at repack.cpp:51 (its own comment says `// scalar`). Disassembled it in bin-d4 at 0x3d8560: a 9-instruction-per-element amax loop, then a second per-element loop that calls out of line to `__roundf` (0x55ad24, 11 instructions including frflags/fsflags). Pristine arm: Q1_0's vec_dot_type is GGML_TYPE_Q8_0 (ggml-cpu.c:256), whose from_float is `quantize_row_q8_0` (ggml-cpu.c:298); ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat quantizes every src1 row with it (ggml-cpu.c:1363/1376) and has no 4-row batched path at all. Disassembled it in bin-pristine at 0x4250a8: 30 RVV instructions per 32-element block (vle32/vfabs/vfredmax/vfmul.vf/vfncvt/vncvt/vse8). The fitted per-call constant F=489,581 for gemm d4 works out to 47.8 cycles per activation element at ne0=2560, i.e. ~6,120 cycles per 32-column block of 4 rows - consistent with ~4,900 scalar instructions per block from the disassembly, and ~17x what the vector loop costs for the same work.
findings.finding: Pristine and the three repack builds do NOT execute the same activation-quantization code for the same 4 rows x ne10 floats. This is a genuine A/B asymmetry, and it runs AGAINST the optimized build. Scaling the measured F by ne0, the scalar quantizer is 60% of 27B attn_v/attn_k's d4 cycles, 18-19% of ffn_down's, 17-18% of ssm_out/attn_output's, 16% of attn_gate's, 9-11% of attn_qkv/attn_q's and 6-7% of ffn_gate/ffn_up's - while it is under 0.5% of the corresponding pristine numbers. The document describes the scalar quantizer at length but frames it as a gemm-vs-gemv property ("decode gets a vector quantizer and prefill gets a scalar one"), never as a pristine-vs-repack one. A reader is left believing upstream prefill pays the same tax. It does not.
findings.impact: Changes headline numbers, in the optimization's favour. Substituting pristine's vector quantizer for the scalar one (sensitivity-tested at 42-48 cycles/element of penalty) moves the published per-node totals to: attn_v 11.40x -> 24.1-28.5x, attn_k 11.40x -> 24.1-28.6x, ffn_down 22.44x -> 27.1-27.9x, attn_output 18.90x -> 22.6-23.2x, ssm_out 18.86x -> 22.4-23.0x, attn_gate 19.11x -> 22.5-23.1x, attn_qkv 20.25x -> 22.4-22.7x, attn_q 20.75x -> 22.6-22.8x, ffn_gate/ffn_up 21.6x -> 23.0-23.2x. The 10-node geometric mean rises from the published 18.15x to 23.3-24.5x. More important than the level: the corrected values collapse into a 22-29x band, so the doc's "Total speedup tracks node size" note and its 11.40x small-tensor story are largely artifacts of an asymmetry in the optimized build's disfavour, not a property of the kernel.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the Setup or Notes section stating that the upstream leg quantizes activations with the RVV `quantize_row_q8_0` while the repack legs use the scalar `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1`, that this costs the repack legs ~48 cycles per activation element (6-60% of their measured cycles depending on node), and that the published speedups are therefore lower bounds. If a stronger claim is wanted, measure one extra leg: build d4 with the ggml_quantize_mat_t<1,Q8_0> body replaced by four `quantize_row_q8_0` calls and re-run K=57 only (attn_v, the cheapest leg at 1.63M cycles) to pin the correction empirically instead of by fit.

findings.title: "Its vector twin is gated behind __riscv_zvfh" is factually wrong - there is no vector twin, and GGML_RV_ZVFH=ON would change nothing
findings.claim_in_doc: "Its vector twin is gated behind `__riscv_zvfh`, and the measurement build sets `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`." followed by "Vectorizing it is the clearest remaining prefill win."
findings.what_i_checked: `grep -rn quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1 ggml/src/` returns exactly six hits and no arch-specific definition: repack.cpp:51 (the scalar definition, named `..._generic`), repack.cpp:348 and :350 (the two arms of the #if at :347), repack.h:208 and :260 (declarations), and arch-fallback.h:221. arch-fallback.h line 221 sits inside the `#elif defined(__riscv)` branch that opens at line 216 and runs to line 255, with no nested zvfh guard, and reads `#define ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1`. repack.cpp includes arch-fallback.h at line 12, before repack.h at line 19, so the macro renames both the declaration at repack.h:260 and the scalar definition at repack.cpp:51 to the arch name. Confirmed in the shipped binaries: `nm -C bin-baseline/bin-prefetch/bin-d4` shows exactly one symbol, `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1` (at 0x3d8528 / 0x3d8560), with no `..._generic` twin - and its disassembly is the scalar loop. Provenance: `git log -L 221,221:ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch-fallback.h` attributes the alias to upstream commit af237f302 (#19121), an ancestor of HEAD.
findings.finding: Both arms of `#if defined(__riscv_zvfh) && defined(__riscv_v)` at repack.cpp:347 resolve to the same scalar function on RISC-V. With ZVFH ON, line 348 calls `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1`, which is the macro-renamed scalar routine from repack.cpp:51; with ZVFH OFF, line 350 calls `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic`, which macro-expands to the identical symbol. The declaration at repack.h:208 under `#if defined __riscv_zvfh` is a promise no arch file keeps. Rebuilding with -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=ON would produce a bit-identical quantizer.
findings.impact: Does not change any published cycle count, but it misdiagnoses the cause of the largest single item the document identifies in a small prefill matmul. A reader acting on the doc would flip a build flag and measure no change. The recommendation itself survives - vectorizing the 4x1 quantizer is still the right next lever, and this audit's own correction shows it is worth 18.15x -> ~24x on the 10-node geomean - but the work required is writing a new RVV kernel, not turning on an extension.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "No vector implementation of this routine exists on RISC-V: `arch-fallback.h:221` aliases the generic scalar definition (`repack.cpp:51`) to the arch name, so both arms of the `#if` at `repack.cpp:347` call the same scalar function and `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=ON` changes nothing. Writing an RVV `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1` in `arch/riscv/repack.cpp` - the 4x8 twin at `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:26` is the template - is the clearest remaining prefill win."

findings.title: The one-time repack cost is never disclosed, and it is 58-141x one measured matmul of the same tensor
findings.claim_in_doc: "Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one MUL_MAT node" and the variant table row "| `baseline` | repack ON ... | + row-parallel 64x1 repack |". The document never mentions when or at what cost the repacked layout is produced.
findings.what_i_checked: Located the conversion: `ggml_backend_cpu_repack_buffer_alloc_buffer` installs `ggml_backend_cpu_repack_buffer_set_tensor` (repack.cpp:4906-4915), which calls `tensor_traits->repack(tensor, data, size)` -> `repack_q1_0_to_q1_0_64_bl` (repack.cpp:3309-3345). That is a buffer set_tensor, driven from the model loader, so it runs entirely before graph execution - the ROI markers live in `ggml_compute_forward` (ggml-cpu.c:1744-1790, 1913) and only fire during graph compute, so none of the repack lands inside the ROI. Sized it two ways. (a) Disassembly: the routine's innermost loop in bin-d4 (0x3cdd30-0x3cdd74) is 18 scalar instructions with two loads and a byte read-modify-write store, and it executes exactly nrow*ne0 times, i.e. once per weight element. (b) Empirically from the logs' own timestamps: model load (`load the model` -> `llama threadpool init`) is 162.1 s mean over the 12 pristine legs (min 158.0, max 166.1, spread 2.5%) versus 460.4 / 504.8 / 488.3 s mean for baseline / prefetch / d4 - a ~3.0x, ~320 s inflation with no other difference in the load path.
findings.finding: The measured cycles exclude a real one-time cost of roughly 18 instructions per weight element. At IPC 0.67-1.0 that is 94-142M cycles for attn_v (5.24M weights) and 1.60-2.41 billion cycles for ffn_down or ffn_gate (89.1M weights each) - i.e. 58-141x ONE measured d4 matmul of the same tensor and 4.2-7.8x one upstream matmul of it. Excluding it is legitimate: it is an amortized load-time conversion, upstream llama.cpp does exactly the same through the same hook for q4_0_4x4/8x8, q4_K, q5_K, q6_K, iq4_nl, mxfp4 and q8_0 (the hook is upstream commit f470bc36b, untouched by this branch), and break-even against upstream comes after only 4.4-8.4 four-token prefill passes over a tensor - about 18-34 prompt tokens. But it is invisible to the reader, and the ~3x load-time inflation is sitting in every log the document ships as evidence.
findings.impact: Does not change any published speedup. It changes what the speedups mean for a short prompt: a single 4-token prefill of one layer is net SLOWER with the repack than without it, and the document's framing ("nothing here is inferred") invites the reader to treat 20x as an end-to-end figure it is not.
findings.fix: Add a bullet to Notes: "The 64x1 layout is built once at model load in `ggml_backend_cpu_repack_buffer_set_tensor` (`repack.cpp:4906`), outside the ROI, as upstream does for its own repack types. It costs 18 scalar instructions per weight element - about 1.6-2.4 billion cycles for a 17408x5120 tensor - and break-evens against upstream after roughly 5-8 four-token prefill passes over that tensor. Model load in these logs goes from 162 s (pristine) to ~480 s (repack)."

findings.title: "F stays put" is contradicted by the document's own table: gemm F rises 23%, gemv F rises 195%

findings.title: The fit's goodness-of-fit is quoted for gemv, but the load-bearing constant comes from the gemm fit, whose residual is 5x worse
findings.claim_in_doc: "Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles` (gemv residuals within 1.1%)" - immediately above the table whose gemm `d4` row (F = 489,581) is then used for "12.4x the per-call fixed cost", "59% of 4B `attn_v`'s total" and "at ~490K cycles per node it is the largest single item in a small prefill matmul".
findings.what_i_checked: Recomputed max |residual| for every fit: gemv pristine 1.46%, baseline 0.28%, prefetch 0.11%, d4 1.14%; gemm pristine 1.87%, baseline 0.21%, prefetch 0.91%, d4 5.19%. result.summary: The instrument is sound in the ways that matter most and the comparison is not rigged: every Setup parameter reproduces exactly from the elaborated RTL config (/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax46mpv_fpga_l3/obj_sc/config.inc: NDS_VLEN 1024, NDS_NHART 1, ICACHE/DCACHE 32 KB, L2C 0, L3C 2048 KB), the engine really is Verilator-elaborated Andes RTL, and disassembly of the four k57 binaries shows the A/B knobs are physically present and exclusive (vd4dots 64x only in d4, in-kernel prefetch.r only in prefetch/d4, identical ISA attribute strings except d4's added xandesvdot1p0). The VLEN dispute is settled in the document's favour: ggml-cpu.c:768 stores __riscv_vlenb(), which is BYTES, so the log's "RVV_VLEN = 128" means 128 bytes = 1024 bits, and bin-prefetch-k57 contains a live "csrr t1,vlenb; li s3,127; bltu s3,t1" dispatch that can only have taken the VLEN-1024 branch. Two instrument facts are undisclosed and both cut against the optimization rather than for it: main memory behind the 2 MB L3 is an idealised 1-cycle SystemC TLM model (vsim_andesim/src/platform/simple_memory.hpp:40, main.cpp:200 default 1, never overridden by andesim), so "Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement" overstates and the +prefetch stage's 1.05-1.08x is a floor rather than a transferable figure; and the ROI brackets a single cold first call in which the three optimized builds pay a scalar activation quantizer (repack.cpp:4460) that pristine never pays (fitted per-call fixed cost on 27B: pristine 312,358 vs 824,191/920,157/895,692), so subtracting a common fixed cost moves attn_v from 11.40x to 13.86x. The real weaknesses are determinism and reproduction: --selfcheck re-runs nothing once its logs exist, its tolerance is +/-1% against constants taken 2026-08-01 with an ROI marker not committed until 2026-08-07, no controlled repeat of any binary exists anywhere, the best same-code spread available is 0.30-0.46% (the four ssm_alpha/ssm_beta builds), the repo's two published values for the same 4B K=51 d4 decode node differ by 5.12% (362,799 vs 381,355), and the entire 27B decode column this document compares against has no logs on disk and no reproduction command.
