findings.what_i_checked: Traced the vsim platform. /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/platform/platform.hpp:53 instantiates `SimpleMemory<data_width> main_memory` and binds it to the interconnect (:86-89). /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/platform/simple_memory.hpp:40 `unsigned latency = 1;` -- every read and write, regardless of address, size, bank or row, returns `latency`, and b_transport (:62-67) adds `sc_time(cycles, SC_NS)`. The clock is `sc_clock clk{"clk", sc_core::sc_time{1, SC_NS}}` (platform.hpp:39), so 1 ns = 1 cycle. /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp:200 documents `--mem-latency <cycles>  Memory access latency in cycles [default: 1]`; `grep -rn "mem-latency" /home/nick/work/andesim` returns nothing, so andesim never overrides the default. The interconnect (src/platform/interconnect.hpp:118) forwards b_transport without adding delay.
findings.finding: The core, its L1s and the 2 MB L3 are genuine Verilator-elaborated RTL, but everything past the L3 -- what the document calls DRAM when it reasons about "miss latency" -- is a flat 1-cycle C++ model with no row activation, no bank conflict, no refresh, no bandwidth ceiling and no queueing. "Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement" is therefore true of the pipeline and cache hierarchy and false of the memory system. This is not fatal to the ratios: at d4 the largest node moves 12.53 MB in 14,351,598 cycles = 0.87 bytes/cycle, and the smallest 0.72 MB in 1,630,251 = 0.45 bytes/cycle, so no variant is anywhere near a realistic bandwidth wall and both sides of every A/B stream the same weight bytes. But the +prefetch stage exists solely to hide miss latency, and on this engine there is almost none to hide -- so its measured 1.05-1.08x is a lower bound on silicon, not a transferable number, and the mechanism sentence quoted above is being argued on a memory model that does not implement the mechanism.
findings.impact: No headline ratio changes. The +repack (6.98x) and +vd4dots (2.76x) stages are essentially unaffected because neither is bandwidth-limited here. The +prefetch stage (1.07x geomean, the smallest of the three) is the one number in the document that would be expected to grow, not shrink, on real silicon, and the document's own explanation of it rests on latency the simulator does not model. Absolute cycle counts are optimistic for all four variants by an unknown amount.
findings.fix: Add one line to the Setup table: "memory behind the L3 is a flat 1-cycle TLM model (`vsim_andesim/src/platform/simple_memory.hpp:40`, `--mem-latency` default 1), so absolute cycles are optimistic and the +prefetch stage is a lower bound." If a stronger claim is wanted, re-run two legs (baseline and prefetch on ffn_gate) with `--mem-latency 40` and report how 1.08x moves.

findings.title: The scalar activation quantizer is charged only to the optimized builds, and the document calls it "shared"
findings.claim_in_doc: "`F` is not part of the kernel... It is the shared activation path, and the source says what it is." and "So decode gets a vector quantizer and prefill gets a scalar one. That is the whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap" (Why prefill loses its edge on small tensors)
findings.what_i_checked: Read both quantize sites. The repack path (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:4456-4469) sends the 4-token group through `ggml_quantize_mat_t<INTER_SIZE, PARAM_TYPE>` and only the ne11 % 4 remainder through `from_float`. The upstream path (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:1299 and :1363) uses `from_float` = `quantize_row_q8_0` for every token, which is RVV-vectorized on RISC-V (arch/riscv/quants.c:32). pristine sets GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF, so `ggml_cpu_extra_compute_forward` returns false and pristine takes the upstream path. Then I fitted cycles = F + T*rows over the seven 27B ne0=5120 nodes, per variant.
findings.finding: pristine's fitted per-call fixed cost is 312,358 cycles (max residual 0.98%); baseline 824,191 (0.50%), prefetch 920,157 (2.57%), d4 895,692 (3.94%). The ~510-610K gap is the scalar 4x1 quantizer that only the three optimized builds run. So the fixed cost is *not* "the shared activation path" -- the before gets the fast quantizer and the after gets the slow one, on every one of the ten optimizable nodes. The direction of the bias is against the optimization, so the comparison is not rigged in the paper's favour; but the document's own diagnosis of its weakest result (attn_v/attn_k at 11.40x) is built on a constant it wrongly describes as common to all four builds.
findings.impact: Every published ratio is conservative. Subtracting pristine's own fixed cost from both sides as a sensitivity: attn_v 11.40x -> 13.86x (+22%), attn_k 11.40x -> 13.87x, attn_output 18.90x -> 19.83x (+5%), ffn_gate 21.57x -> 22.03x (+2%), ffn_down 22.44x -> 22.84x (+2%). The layer-6 geomean would rise from 20.60x to roughly 21x. No headline number is overstated; the small-node story is understated by about a fifth.
findings.fix: Change "It is the shared activation path" to state which builds pay it, and add pristine to the F/T table (27B: F = 312,358 vs 824,191 / 920,157 / 895,692). One sentence in the attn_v discussion: "the optimized builds pay a scalar quantizer that upstream does not, so 11.40x is a floor -- net of a common fixed cost it is 13.9x."

findings.title: --selfcheck is not a determinism gate: it re-runs nothing once the logs exist, and its constants come from a pre-ROI-commit revision
findings.claim_in_doc: sweep.sh header: "the cycle figure comes from a cycle-accurate RTL model, so host load cannot move it. --selfcheck proves both claims at once by running two legs together and comparing each against its published value." The document repeats it: "bash sweep.sh --selfcheck     # gate: re-derive two published attn_v numbers" (Reproducing)
findings.what_i_checked: Read selfcheck() (sweep.sh) and the run_leg() it calls. run_leg's resume guard is `if [ -f "$log" ] && grep -q '^\[andesim\] .* cycles' "$log" && grep -q '\[roi\] MUL_MAT' "$log"; then echo "have"; return 0`. Both target logs exist and are complete (sweep-gemm/prefetch-k51.log, sweep-gemm/d4-k51.log). Read the tolerance: `awk 'BEGIN{exit !(g>w*0.99 && g<w*1.01)}'` = +/-1%. Traced the constants: 1,651,949 and 818,314 are opt_roadmap.md F8/F9, "MEASURED" 2026-08-01. `git log --format="%h %ad"` shows the current ROI marker was not committed until 1c233145c, 2026-08-07, and the k51 binaries are dated 2026-08-19. Read sweep-selfcheck.out.
findings.finding: Three separate problems. (1) It ran exactly once (sweep-selfcheck.out shows "run", not "have"); every subsequent invocation -- including any a third party makes today -- short-circuits on the resume guard and compares two stored files to two stored constants, simulating nothing. (2) The tolerance is +/-1%, and the one real run landed at 0.052% (prefetch: 1,651,086 vs 1,651,949) and 0.62% (d4: 823,397 vs 818,314), i.e. ~19x and ~1.6x margin, so it is not calibrated to any measured noise floor. (3) Even that one run was not a determinism test: the reference constants were taken with an ROI marker that did not exist in any commit until six days later, so the 0.62% conflates run-to-run variation, marker placement and binary drift with no way to separate them. The header claim "host load cannot move it... --selfcheck proves both claims at once" is therefore unsupported by the script as written.
findings.impact: Does not change any published cycle count. It removes the document's only advertised determinism evidence, which matters because the smallest reported stage (+prefetch, 1.05-1.08x = 5-8%) is the one that needs an error bar.
findings.fix: Give selfcheck a `FORCE=1` path that deletes the two logs before run_leg, and change its references to two numbers produced by the *current* binaries. Better: add a genuine repeat -- run one leg (d4 k=57, ~1.6M cycles, minutes) twice from the same binary and publish the delta as the noise floor. Then set the tolerance from it.

findings.title: No controlled repeat exists; the only two same-node comparisons in the repo disagree by 0.62% and 5.12%
findings.claim_in_doc: "Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement" (line 7), with all three stage ratios reported to two decimals and per-node prefetch discrimination of 1.05x vs 1.08x.
findings.what_i_checked: Searched every log directory for a repeated leg: none exists (48 fresh runs in sweep-gemm-27b.out, zero "have" lines, no BAD-NROWS or non-zero exits). Compared the two independently published values for the same 4B K=51 node: prefill d4 818,314 (opt_roadmap F9 / sweep.sh selfcheck constant) vs 823,397 (sweep-gemm/d4-k51.log) = 0.62%; decode d4 362,799 (opt_roadmap F9 and the q1_0_reproduce.md Level-4 table) vs 381,355 (sweep-gemv/d4-k51.log) = 5.12%. Then measured the best same-code spread available: ssm_alpha (K=49) runs an identical stock kernel in all four binaries -- 936,969 / 939,289 / 939,798 / 938,688 = 0.30% spread; ssm_beta 949,957 / 947,611 / 947,471 / 945,595 = 0.46%. Also found the caveat the repo does record: q1_0_reproduce.md Level 4, "cycles will vary by a fraction of a percent run to run; the ratios are what matters".
findings.finding: There is no repeat measurement of any binary anywhere in the repo, so run-to-run determinism is asserted, never demonstrated. The two cross-revision comparisons that do exist disagree by 0.62% (prefill) and 5.12% (decode) -- the latter far outside the "fraction of a percent" that q1_0_reproduce.md itself promises, and unexplained. The tightest defensible error bar is the four-binary ssm_alpha/ssm_beta spread of 0.30-0.46%, which measures code-layout sensitivity between binaries -- exactly the right error bar for a between-binary A/B like +prefetch. Against that, the three stages are 6.98x, 1.07x and 2.76x: the repack and vd4dots conclusions are 15x and 400x the spread and are safe; the +prefetch stage at 5-8% is 11-27x the spread and also survives, but the document's finer claim that prefetch varies 1.05x to 1.08x across nodes rests on a 2.8-point spread against a 0.30-0.46% instrument spread, i.e. only 6-9x margin.
findings.impact: No published number is shown to be wrong. It means the document has no stated uncertainty, and the smallest of its three stages is reported with two decimals it has not earned. Nothing here threatens the 20.60x or the layer-6 stage split.
findings.fix: Publish the ssm_alpha/ssm_beta four-build spread (0.30% and 0.46%) as the between-binary floor -- the data is already in the tables -- and carry q1_0_reproduce.md's own caveat ("cycles will vary by a fraction of a percent run to run; the ratios are what matters") into this document's Setup. Separately, run d4 k=57 twice and record the true same-binary delta.

findings.claim_in_doc: "Regenerate any table with `MODEL=27b NODES=\"...\" bash sweep.sh --md`" (line 9-10), plus the head-to-head table (decode 2.24x / 1.60x / 3.54x / 12.64x), the 10-node 12.20x, the per-layer 12.53x / 12.17x, and the 12-row "Per-node comparison, prefill vs decode" table.

This document's Reproducing block gives 27B prefill commands and 4B commands only.
findings.finding: Every decode number in this document is quoted from a sibling write-up whose primary evidence is not in the repository. A third party can regenerate the prefill side exactly (I did) and can regenerate nothing on the decode side. findings.title: The upstream comparator uses 32 of the machine's 128 vector lanes, and this document never says so
findings.claim_in_doc: "| `pristine` | `GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF` | upstream llama.cpp |" and "| `prefetch` | ... = **standard RVV** |", with the headline "Geometric mean over the layer's 6 optimizable nodes: **20.60x**"
findings.what_i_checked: Read the baseline kernel. ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c:563-574 dispatches any VLEN >= 256 to `ggml_vec_dot_q1_0_q8_0_vl256`, whose body (:493-494) does `const size_t vl32 = __riscv_vsetvl_e8m1(32); assert(vl32 == 32);` and then runs vle8/vneg/vmerge/vwredsum at vl=32 with a horizontal `vwredsum` every 32 elements. On VLEN=1024 the e8m1 VLMAX is 128, so 96 of 128 lanes are idle. Cross-checked against the repo's own analysis: q1_0_layout_rvv_vs_vd4dot.md:102-124, "The VLEN=1024 limitation of upstream ... 75 percent of potential i8 lanes are idle at VLEN=1024, and the kernel performs a horizontal reduction plus scalar-scale work four times for every 128-K Q1_0 block."
findings.finding: The baseline is genuine unmodified upstream llama.cpp, so this is not rigging -- it is the right comparator for "what does upstream get on this chip today". But a material share of the 20.60x is a property of running a 32-lane algorithm on a 128-lane machine, not of the optimization, and the same 20.60x would be much smaller on a VLEN=256 part where the upstream kernel is at full lane utilisation. This document presents the ratio as a property of the optimization and labels the second build "standard RVV" without anywhere disclosing that the *first* build is not standard-RVV-tuned for this VLEN. The repo already documents the fact in a sibling file; this write-up neither links it nor restates it.
findings.impact: Does not change any measured cycle count or any ratio computed here. It changes how the headline generalises: 20.60x is specific to VLEN=1024, and a reader is given no way to see that. The fitted upstream cost (17,800 cycles per row at K=5120) is consistent with a kernel doing one horizontal reduction per 32 elements, which is the mechanism named in the sibling doc.
findings.fix: Add two sentences after the build-variant table: "`pristine` is upstream's VLEN>=256 path (`arch/riscv/quants.c:563`), which pins vl=32 and reduces horizontally every 32 elements, so on this VLEN=1024 engine it uses 32 of 128 i8 lanes -- see q1_0_layout_rvv_vs_vd4dot.md. Part of the ratio below is that gap, and it would be smaller at VLEN=256."

findings.title: The measured window is a single cold first call, and every ratio is shrunk by a variant-independent constant
findings.claim_in_doc: "Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one MUL_MAT node" (line 7); the Setup gives no indication that the node is executed once, cold.
findings.what_i_checked: andesim/docs/USER_GUIDE.md:25-27: "QEMU races through boot and setup, then hands the complete architectural state and memory to the cycle-accurate engine". QEMU models no caches, TLBs or branch predictors, and the state-transport document (andesim/docs/hybrid_state_transport_problems.md, M1-M6) covers only CSRs and MMIO device registers -- nothing restores cache contents. Combined with the static counter (ggml-cpu.c:1746, never reset), `--no-warmup`, and K=48..59 all falling in the first forward pass, the measurement is one cold first-touch execution.
findings.finding: This is symmetric in kind -- all four variants get the same cold start -- but not in magnitude: a roughly constant absolute cost is a much larger share of a fast run than a slow one, so it compresses every reported ratio. I bounded it: the cold-start component cannot exceed pristine's whole fitted fixed cost, 312,358 cycles on 27B (which also contains pristine's vector quantizer, so 312K is a loose upper bound). The I-cache part specifically is negligible -- the kernels are 1.4-1.6 KB in a 32 KB I$ and d4 is only 70 bytes larger than prefetch. The one place a cold window could flatter the after is +prefetch: a cold cache maximises compulsory misses and denies the hardware D-cache prefetcher (config.inc:338-340, 4 entries) time to lock onto a stream. I cannot size that from what is on disk.
findings.impact: Bounded and conservative. Removing a common 312,358-cycle constant from both sides moves attn_v 11.40x -> 13.86x (+22%), attn_output 18.90x -> 19.83x (+5%), ffn_gate 21.57x -> 22.03x (+2%), ffn_down 22.44x -> 22.84x (+2%). So the published figures understate by ~2% on the large nodes and ~22% on the two small ones. The residual worry about +prefetch and the hardware prefetcher is unquantified and points the other way.
findings.fix: State in Setup that the ROI brackets one cold first execution and that the ratios are therefore floors. To close the +prefetch sub-question, run the A/B that build.sh already supports: `bash build.sh prefetch-nodpref baseline-nodpref` (which clears mcache_ctl.DPREF_EN inside the ROI, ggml-cpu.c:1755-1775) on one node -- if the software-prefetch gain survives with the hardware prefetcher off, the cold window is not what is producing it.

findings.title: ZVFH is switched off in software although the engine has vector FP16 in hardware
findings.claim_in_doc: "Its vector twin is gated behind `__riscv_zvfh`, and the measurement build sets `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`." and "Vectorizing it is the clearest remaining prefill win."
findings.what_i_checked: build.sh cfg() passes -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF to all four variants (so it is not an A/B bias). The elaborated RTL header /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax46mpv_fpga_l3/obj_sc/config.inc:76-77 sets `NDS_VECTOR_PACKED_FP16_SUPPORT "yes"` / `..._INT 1`. Also note repack.cpp:4753 gates a whole family of repack types behind `#if defined __riscv_zvfh`.
findings.finding: The document discloses the flag but not that the hardware underneath it exists. A reader is left to assume the scalar quantizer is forced by the engine; it is forced by the build. Since ZVFH=OFF is applied identically to all four builds it biases no A/B -- it adds a common ~500K-900K constant that, like the cold start, makes every ratio conservative. I could not establish from anything on disk whether Andes "packed FP16" is exactly RVV Zvfh as the toolchain spells it, so the inference that flipping the flag would just work is not verified.
findings.impact: No ratio changes. It understates how cheap the document's own recommended next step is: "the clearest remaining prefill win" may be a build flag on this engine rather than new code.
findings.fix: Add to Setup: "-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF on all four builds, although the engine reports NDS_VECTOR_PACKED_FP16_SUPPORT=yes -- so the scalar quantizer below is a build choice, not a hardware limit." Then run one leg of `d4` on attn_v with ZVFH=ON to confirm the vector quantizer path compiles and to size the win.

findings.title: The gemm fixed-cost fit is much softer than the document implies
findings.claim_in_doc: "Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles` (gemv residuals within 1.1%)" then "| gemm `d4` (4 tok) | 489,581 | 23,036 | **5,759** |" and "`F` is 59% of 4B `attn_v`'s total and only 12% of its `ffn_gate`."
findings.what_i_checked: Refitted from sweep-gemm/ and sweep-gemv/. All six published (F, T) pairs reproduce exactly. But the residuals differ sharply by path: gemv max residual is 0.3% / 0.1% / 1.1% (baseline / prefetch / d4), while gemm is 0.2% / 0.9% / **5.2%**. The document quotes only the gemv figure. I then re-derived F from individual node pairs of the gemm d4 data: attn_v+ffn_gate gives F = 452,901; attn_v+attn_q gives 407,381; attn_q+ffn_gate gives 688,731.
findings.finding: The single number the whole "scalar quantizer" argument rests on, gemm d4 F = 489,581, is only determined to roughly +/-30% by the five data points behind it, and the document discloses the residual only for the path where the fit is tight. "F is 59% of 4B attn_v's total" is really 49%-84%; "12.4x the per-call fixed cost" inherits the same width. The qualitative conclusion -- prefill carries an order-of-magnitude larger per-call constant than decode, and it is the scalar quantizer -- is well supported (my independent 27B fit gives the same picture, and the pristine-vs-repack gap of 510-610K confirms the mechanism). Only the precision is overstated.
findings.impact: Changes no headline ratio. It weakens the sharpness of the section's numbers: the two-decimal presentation (489,581; 12.4x; 59%) implies precision the five-point fit does not carry.
findings.fix: Quote the gemm residual alongside the gemv one ("gemv within 1.1%, gemm d4 within 5.2%") and round the derived claims: "F is roughly half a million cycles, about half to four-fifths of 4B attn_v's total, an order of magnitude above decode's."

findings.title: "27B tensors are far larger than the 2 MB L3" is false for the two nodes the sentence is used to explain
findings.claim_in_doc: "**Prefetch is worth slightly more here than on 4B** (1.05-1.08x vs 1.03-1.05x). 27B tensors are far larger than the 2 MB L3, so more miss latency survives the M-tile reuse." (Notes)
findings.what_i_checked: Computed weight bytes (weights x 1.125 / 8) and the baseline/prefetch ratio for all ten optimizable 27B nodes: attn_v 0.74 MB / 1.0509, attn_k 0.74 / 1.0501, attn_output 4.42 / 1.0518, ssm_out 4.42 / 1.0548, attn_gate 4.42 / 1.0673, attn_qkv 7.37 / 1.0683, attn_q 8.85 / 1.0640, ffn_down 12.53 / 1.0668, ffn_gate 12.53 / 1.0783, ffn_up 12.53 / 1.0784. Cross-checked against opt_roadmap.md:526, which records the same caveat for the 4B case: "attn_v's 360 KB working set FITS fpga_l3's 2 MB L3."
findings.finding: attn_v and attn_k are 0.74 MB each -- comfortably inside the 2 MB L3 -- so the blanket statement is wrong for two of the ten nodes. The underlying mechanism survives and is in fact supported by those two nodes: they are the two lowest prefetch gains in the set. But the correlation is weak elsewhere: at an identical 4.42 MB, attn_output gets 1.052 and attn_gate 1.067, a 1.5-point scatter against a total spread of 2.8 points, so tensor size explains only part of the variation.
findings.impact: No number changes. One sentence of mechanism is overstated, and the supporting correlation is weaker than the sentence implies.
findings.fix: Rewrite as: "the largest tensors (12.5 MB ffn_*) get 1.078x and the two that fit the 2 MB L3 (attn_v/attn_k, 0.74 MB) get 1.050x, consistent with more miss latency surviving on the big ones -- though nodes of identical size still differ by 1.5 points."

findings.title: "Regenerate any table with sweep.sh --md" does not hold for the layer-7 table
findings.claim_in_doc: "Regenerate any table with `MODEL=27b NODES=\"...\" bash sweep.sh --md`." (line 9-10) and "MODEL=27b NODES=\"56 57 58 59\" bash sweep.sh --md   # layer 7" (Reproducing)
findings.what_i_checked: Ran the exact command (verified read-only first: md() only calls read_leg(), which cats existing logs). It emits a 4-row table, an ALL-4 row of 378,118,875 / 56,300,390 / 53,185,442 / 20,258,726, and geomeans 6.12x / 1.05x / 2.33x = **15.02x**. The published layer-7 table has 7 rows, a LAYER row of 1,380,604,045 / 241,152,929 / 225,336,152 / 66,024,863, and 17.65x. The layer-6 command, by contrast, reproduces its table exactly.
findings.finding: The command a third party is told to run for layer 7 produces a materially different table from the published one, because three rows are carried by hand from layer 6 and the tool has no way to know that. The document does say the ffn_* rows are carried, but the Reproducing section presents the command without that qualification and "any table" is untrue. (The published LAYER row's +repack and +prefetch cells are also wrong by 23.6% -- already established by the lead auditor -- so a reader following the instructions hits three different mismatches at once with no way to tell which is the error.)
findings.impact: No cycle count changes. It makes the document's own reproduction instructions fail on one of its two main tables, which is the single most likely way a third party would first encounter the layer-7 LAYER-row error.
findings.fix: Change the layer-7 line to `MODEL=27b NODES="56 57 58 59" bash sweep.sh --md   # layer 7, measured nodes only -- 15.02x over 4; the published table adds the 3 carried ffn_* rows from layer 6` and fix the two LAYER cells to 195,052,238 and 182,336,759.

findings.title: The measured binaries predate HEAD and no commit is pinned
findings.claim_in_doc: "Generated 2026-08-31." -- no source revision is recorded anywhere in the document.
findings.what_i_checked: `ls -la bin-*-k57` shows the 27B binaries were built 2026-08-24 13:48-13:55. `git log --format="%h %ad" --date=short` puts the most recent source commit, f480bccff ("refactor(riscv): spell out D4 as VD4DOT"), at 2026-08-27 -- after the build. Confirmed in the binaries: bin-d4-k57's symbols are still `_ZL19q1_gemv_64d4_vl1024...` / `_ZL19q1_gemm_64d4_vl1024...`, the pre-rename names. `git status --porcelain ggml/src/ggml-cpu/` is clean, so HEAD's source is intact.
findings.impact: None on any number. It is one more thing a reproducer has to guess, and it means the codegen gate names in check-vd4dots.sh / opt_roadmap no longer match the symbols in the binaries that produced the tables.
findings.finding: The published numbers come from a tree three days older than HEAD. f480bccff's own message says "Structural change only - a rename, no behavior change", and I found nothing to contradict that, so the numbers are very likely still valid at HEAD -- but a third party rebuilding today gets differently-named symbols than the gates and the roadmap describe, and has no recorded revision to check out.

result.summary: The honest whole-model prefill MUL_MAT speedup for Bonsai-27B is **20.8x** (94,567,922,743 -> 4,554,803,352 cycles across all 497 MUL_MAT nodes), and it is robust: charging the LM head as a 4-token gemm, a 2-token gemv, a 1-token gemv, or omitting it entirely spans only 20.33x-20.76x. That is **14% HIGHER than the document's 18.15x headline**, so the aggregation the doc chose (geometric mean over nodes) is conservative, not flattering - the geomean gives the two 1024-row nodes at 11.40x the same vote as ffn_down at 22.44x, while cycle-weighting gives the big nodes their real 94% share. Decomposing the gap from 18.15x: geometric-to-cycle-weighted is +13.3% (20.57x), layer multiplicity +2.5% (21.09x), the un-repacked ssm_alpha/ssm_beta -2.0% (20.67x, they are 1.99% of the optimized model-wide budget), and the LM head +0.4% (20.76x). The one thing the document never says is that the LM head - `output.weight`, 5120 x 248,320, **4.96% of all matmul weights, larger than 3.3 whole layers** - exists at all; it clears the `ne[1] % 64 == 0` gate only because 248320 is divisible by 64, and had it missed as it does on Bonsai-4B and Bonsai-8B (151669 % 64 = 53) the whole-model figure would collapse from 20.8x to **10.77x**. Finally this is strictly an upper bound: no non-MUL_MAT cycle count exists anywhere in the repo (opt_roadmap.md:744-745 still lists full-token latency as future FPGA work), and at a 95% MUL_MAT share the end-to-end prefill speedup would be 10.4x, not 20.8x.

verified_ok.claim: The LM head passes the repack dispatch gate on this model.
verified_ok.evidence: ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:4889 requires `__riscv_vlenb() * 8 >= 512 && cur->ne[1] % 64 == 0 && cur->ne[0] % QK1_0 == 0`. output.weight is [5120 x 248320]; 248320 % 64 == 0 (=3880 tiles), 5120 % 128 == 0 (QK1_0=128, ggml-common.h:180), and vlenb=128 bytes -> 1024 bits >= 512. All three hold.

findings.title: The document never gives an end-to-end number; the honest whole-model MUL_MAT figure is 20.8x, higher than every headline it does give
findings.claim_in_doc: "Over prefill's full set of 10 optimizable nodes the totals are 6.62x / 1.06x / 2.58x = **18.15x**" (line 124-126); "Geometric mean over the layer's 6 optimizable nodes: **20.60x**" (line 47). No sentence anywhere states a model-wide or end-to-end prefill speedup.
findings.what_i_checked: Built it from primary evidence. Layer sets from the logs (layer 6 = 8 nodes as measured; layer 7 = 4 measured + 3 carried, using the TRUE totals 1,380,604,045 / 195,052,238 / 182,336,759 / 66,024,863, not the doc's two wrong cells). Layer multiplicity from the gguf: 48 x layer-6 set + 16 x layer-7 set = 90,147,464,608 pristine / 4,360,522,544 d4. LM head from a `cycles = F + T*rows` least-squares fit over the seven ne0=5120 nodes (pristine F=312,358 T=17,800.2/row, max residual 0.98%; d4 F=895,692 T=778.8/row, max residual 3.94%), evaluated at 248,320 rows: 4,420,458,135 / 194,280,808.
findings.finding: Whole model, all 497 MUL_MAT nodes: pristine 94,567,922,743 -> d4 4,554,803,352 = **20.76x**, staged 7.04x / 1.07x / 2.76x. The result is insensitive to how the LM head is charged: nrows=4 gemm 20.76x, nrows=2 gemv 20.33x, ~1-token 20.50x, head omitted 20.67x; even a 2x error in the head extrapolation moves it to 20.84x. The gap from 18.15x decomposes as: geometric -> cycle-weighted over the SAME 10 shapes +13.3% (18.15x -> 20.57x), + layer multiplicity +2.5% (-> 21.09x), + ssm_alpha/ssm_beta -2.0% (-> 20.67x), + LM head +0.4% (-> 20.76x).
findings.impact: Adds the number the reader most needs and it is favourable: 20.8x, not 18.15x. The doc's headline understates its own model-wide MUL_MAT result by 14%. Layer 6's 20.60x turns out to be an almost exact proxy for the whole model; the 18.15x 10-node figure is not.
findings.fix: Add one table row: "whole model, all 497 MUL_MAT nodes (48 x layer 6 + 16 x layer 7 + LM head): 94,567,922,743 -> 4,554,803,352 = 20.76x cycle-weighted", with a footnote that the LM head term is extrapolated, not measured, and that the two geomeans are per-node averages, not model totals.

findings.title: The LM head - 4.96% of all matmul weights - is never mentioned, and it clears the 64-row gate only by luck; on 4B and 8B it does not, and the model-wide result would be 10.77x
findings.claim_in_doc: "`ssm_alpha` and `ssm_beta` are the only two tensors in the model the kernel is never applied to." (line 64-65) and "Every layer in the model is one of two kinds, so measuring one of each covers the whole model" (line 22-24). The word `output`, `lm_head` or `vocab` appears nowhere in the document.
findings.what_i_checked: Read the gguf tensor table. `output.weight` is [5120 x 248320] Q1_0 = 1,271,398,400 weights, a separate tensor from `token_embd.weight` (no tying). Model-wide matmul weights = 48 x 383,221,760 + 16 x 372,244,480 + 1,271,398,400 = 25,621,954,560, so the head is 4.96% of them - bigger than 3.3 complete layers. Checked the gate at repack.cpp:4889 for all three models.
findings.finding: "Measuring one of each layer kind covers the whole model" is not true: it leaves out the single largest tensor. The head is MUL_MAT node #497, it has never been measured (no `bin-*-k497` exists; no `bin-*-k60/61/62` either), and it PASSES the gate only because 248320 % 64 == 0. Bonsai-4B and Bonsai-8B both have 151,669-row heads (151669 % 64 = 53) which FAIL - so the very sensitivity the doc spends a paragraph on for ssm_alpha/ssm_beta applies with 5,200x more weight to a tensor it never names, and 27B happens to be the one model of the three where it lands the right way. If it had failed, the head would sit at 1.00x and be 50.3% of the optimized MUL_MAT budget, dropping the whole model from 20.76x to **10.77x**. Separately, the head runs at 1 token, not 4, in both sweeps: qwen35.cpp:214-222 applies `ggml_get_rows(cur, inp_out_ids)` before `build_lora_mm(model.output, ...)`, and llama-context.cpp:1684 sets `output_all = cparams.embeddings` = false, so n_outputs = 1.
findings.impact: Does not change 20.76x (the head is only +0.4%), but it changes what the result means: the paper's largest single risk is undisclosed, and the headline does not port to the 4B/8B models the rest of the project uses. Correcting the "covers the whole model" sentence is required either way.
findings.fix: Add one line to the Setup or Notes: "`output.weight` (5120 x 248320, 1,271,398,400 weights, 4.96% of the model's matmul weights) is not in either layer; 248320 % 64 == 0 so it does clear the repack gate, but it is extrapolated, not measured. On Bonsai-4B/8B the same tensor has 151,669 rows and fails." Then measure it: `ROI_K=497 bash build.sh <variant>` for the four variants - at an extrapolated 4.42G pristine cycles that is the most expensive leg in the project, so at minimum measure the d4 and prefetch legs and bound pristine.

findings.title: The bound excludes all non-MUL_MAT work and no measurement of it exists anywhere in the project
findings.claim_in_doc: "Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one MUL_MAT node" (line 7-8). Nothing in the document qualifies what fraction of a prefill pass MUL_MAT is.
findings.what_i_checked: Searched opt_roadmap.md, q1_0_reproduce.md, q1_0_layout_rvv_vs_vd4dot.md, q1_0_8b_hybrid.md and all sweep logs for any whole-graph or full-token cycle count. None exists. opt_roadmap.md:744-745 lists it as unfinished work: "FPGA: final full-token latency (libnn-optimizer style flow), per-kernel ROI if a full token is too slow." The [andesim] cycle line brackets exactly one node (ggml-cpu.c:1744-1790, 1913); the llama.cpp wall-clock lines in the logs are functional-mode host time and carry no cycle information.
findings.finding: 20.76x is an upper bound on the end-to-end prefill speedup, and after a 20x MUL_MAT win the residue is what decides the real number. On this architecture the residue is not small in kind: 64 rmsnorms x2, rope, flash-attention over 16 layers, 48 delta-net recurrent scans plus their conv1d, silu/mul, KV writes, and a softmax/sampler over a 248,320-entry vocabulary. Amdahl on the 20.76x kernel figure: MUL_MAT at 99.5% of upstream cycles gives 18.9x end-to-end, 99% gives 17.3x, 98% gives 14.9x, 95% gives 10.4x, 90% gives 7.0x.
findings.impact: Nothing in the document survives being quoted as an end-to-end speedup. The plausible end-to-end range is anywhere from ~7x to ~19x and the project has no evidence to narrow it.
findings.fix: Add the sentence "all figures are MUL_MAT-only; non-MUL_MAT cycles are unmeasured, so these are upper bounds on end-to-end" plus the Amdahl line, and run one whole-graph ROI leg (set GGML_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=1 with GGML_ROI_MUL_MAT_N large enough to span node 1 to node 497 - roi.h already supports a first/last window) at d4 only, to get a MUL_MAT share for the optimized build.

findings.title: The geometric mean is the only aggregation offered, and on prefill it understates the cycle-weighted result by 13.3%
findings.claim_in_doc: "All figures are geometric means over nodes" (line 112); "Over prefill's full set of 10 optimizable nodes the totals are ... **18.15x**" (line 124-126). The word "totals" is used for what is a geometric mean of ratios.
findings.what_i_checked: Computed both over the identical 10 optimizable shapes, one copy each: geomean 18.15x (reproduces the doc), cycle-weighted 1,794,102,780 / 87,210,375 = 20.57x. Read sweep.sh's md() comment, which deliberately refuses to print a cycle-weighted ratio: "NO ratio: sum(upstream)/sum(vd4dots) is a cycle-weighted aggregate, which the big nodes dominate and which reads like a per-node speedup without being one."
findings.finding: The tool's reasoning is correct for a per-node table, and the choice runs AGAINST the author's interest - it is the small 1024-row nodes at 11.40x that drag the geomean down, and cycle-weighting is what the model actually experiences. But the consequence is that the document publishes no aggregate at all while presenting 18.15x with the word "totals", which a reader will naturally take as the model number. It is the largest single term (+13.3%) in the gap between the headline and the true 20.76x. Separately, the word "totals" on line 124 is applied to three geometric means (6.62x / 1.06x / 2.58x).
findings.impact: No headline is wrong and no comparison is rigged - the bias runs in the conservative direction. It costs the reader 2.6x of understated speedup and invites the wrong reading of 18.15x.
findings.fix: Change "the totals are ... 18.15x" to "the geometric means are ... 18.15x", and add the cycle-weighted companion (20.57x over the same 10 shapes) so the reader can see the two answers and which one applies to a model.

findings.title: "Padding them to 64 rows is the cheapest win available on this model" is contradicted by the doc's own quantizer analysis, by 6.6x
findings.claim_in_doc: "They are 0.06% of the layer's weights but **2.7% of its optimized cycles** ... Padding them to 64 rows is the cheapest win available on this model." (lines 222-224) versus "at ~490K cycles per node it is the largest single item in a small prefill matmul ... Vectorizing it is the clearest remaining prefill win." (lines 195-197)
findings.what_i_checked: Model-wide, ssm_alpha+ssm_beta cost 48 x (938,688 + 945,595) = 90,445,584 d4 cycles = 1.99% of the 4,554,803,352 whole-model d4 budget (the doc's 2.7% is layer-6-only and is correct as written for layer 6). The fixed per-call term: my 27B d4 fit gives F = 895,692 at ne0=5120 = 174.9 cycles per input column; summing ne0 over all 497 calls gives 3,396,608 columns, so ~594,202,073 cycles = 13.0% of the same budget. Cross-checked against the doc's own independent 4B fit (489,581 / 2560 = 191.2 cyc/col, 9% apart).
findings.finding: Two sections of the same document each nominate a different "cheapest / clearest" next win, and neither is sized model-wide. Model-wide the scalar activation quantizer is ~6.6x the ssm dead spot (13.0% vs 1.99% of optimized MUL_MAT cycles). "Cheapest" may fairly mean cheapest to implement rather than largest, but as written the two sentences point a reader in opposite directions with no numbers to arbitrate. (Also noted: "0.06% of the layer's weights" is wrong - 2 x 245,760 / 383,221,760 = 0.128%, which is the 0.12% the doc gives correctly at line 72.)
findings.impact: Changes no headline. Changes what a reader does next: padding ssm moves the whole model 20.76x -> 21.16x (+1.9%), whereas eliminating the fixed term would be worth several times that.
findings.fix: Give both a model-wide share in the Notes - "ssm_alpha/ssm_beta 1.99% of the optimized model-wide MUL_MAT budget; the scalar activation quantizer ~13%" - and say which is cheapest to build versus largest to win, rather than calling each one "the" next win.

findings.title: The LAYER rows and both geomeans are hand-assembled; sweep.sh --md never emits them, so nothing checks them
findings.claim_in_doc: "Regenerate any table with `MODEL=27b NODES="..." bash sweep.sh --md`." (lines 9-10), and the Reproducing block at lines 244-248.
findings.what_i_checked: Ran both documented --md commands. Layer 6 emits an "ALL 6" row (1,415,983,905 / 199,828,560 / 186,547,213 / 66,951,649 - only the six gate-passing nodes) and a 20.60x geomean. Layer 7 emits "ALL 4" (378,118,875 / 56,300,390 / 53,185,442 / 20,258,726) and a **15.02x** geomean over the four measured nodes. Neither emits an 8-node or 7-node LAYER row, and neither emits 17.65x.
findings.finding: The command reproduces every measured cell exactly, so the claim holds for the node rows. It does not hold for the bolded LAYER rows or for the 17.65x layer-7 geomean, which are typed by hand from a mix of tool output and carried values - which is precisely where the two 23.6% errors in the layer-7 +repack and +prefetch cells live (published 241,152,929 / 225,336,152 against true 195,052,238 / 182,336,759). Additionally, `bin-pristine-k60/61/62` and `bin-*-k497` do not exist, so a third party cannot measure the carried ffn rows or the LM head without twelve to sixteen new builds; and the doc lists `bash sweep.sh --selfcheck` under "regenerate from logs already on disk", but selfcheck calls run_leg() and would launch two RTL legs on a machine that lacks sweep-gemm/{prefetch,d4}-k51.log (both present here, so it is a no-op read on this machine, and the two legs are small - ~1.65M and ~0.82M cycles).
findings.impact: Explains how the layer-7 error survived and why nothing in the harness caught it. No measured value is affected.
findings.fix: Teach md() to emit a LAYER row (all nodes including gate failures) as well as its ALL-n row, and to accept a carry list so layer 7's ffn_* rows come from the tool rather than from copy-paste. Then regenerate the two tables and the layer-7 geomean from the tool alone.

findings.title: The measured prefill is a 4-token prompt; a real prefill runs 512-token ubatches and none of that regime was measured
findings.claim_in_doc: "Path | prefill / gemm, `nrows=4`" (line 19); "Mode | andesim hybrid, marker trigger, `--no-mmap --mem-size 12G -t 1`" (line 18). Title: "Bonsai-27B prefill".
findings.what_i_checked: sweep.sh sets MODE=gemm via PROMPT="The capital of France" + --no-warmup, giving ne11 = 4; every [roi] line confirms nrows=4. The logs show `n_batch = 2048` and the default n_ubatch is 512, so a production prefill would present ne11 up to 512 to the same nodes.
findings.finding: To first order the result should carry: forward_mul_mat processes 4 tokens per gemm pass, so both the fixed activation-quantize term and the per-tile term scale roughly linearly with token count and their ratio is preserved; and upstream is exactly linear in tokens by the doc's own measurement (line 229-232, `.nrows = 1`). But at ne11=512 the upstream path re-streams the whole weight matrix 512 times against the repacked path's 128, so the observed speedup could grow rather than hold, and cache behaviour at that batch size is entirely unmeasured. Nothing in the repo tests it.
findings.impact: Does not change 20.76x for the measured 4-token pass. Leaves open whether the number is an under- or over-statement for a realistic prompt length; I could not bound the direction from the evidence on disk.
findings.fix: State the token count in the title or the first line ("one forward pass over a 4-token prompt"), and note that ne11=512 behaviour is unmeasured. One cheap check: a single d4 leg at K=53 with a longer prompt would show whether cycles/token stays flat.

result.summary: The 27B decode column is arithmetically sound but evidentially unbacked. Every decode figure quoted in profiling_gemm_27b.md (12.03x/11.86x/.../12.61x per node, 2.24x/1.60x/3.54x/12.64x per stage, 12.53x/12.17x/12.20x geomeans, and the 73,356,044-cycle absolute) re-derives exactly from profiling_gemv_27b.md's cycle counts, and the cross-path sanity check the doc itself proposes is exact (upstream prefill/decode = 1.9724x-2.0116x over all 12 nodes, published as "1.97x to 2.01x"). But there is no `sweep-gemv-27b/` directory: `MODE=gemv MODEL=27b bash sweep.sh --md` prints MISSING for all 12 nodes, so the doc's blanket "Regenerate any table with `MODEL=27b NODES=... bash sweep.sh --md`" is false for every table carrying a decode number, and the Reproducing section gives no decode command at all. The decode runs were made ~5 weeks earlier by a different, now-scratchpad-only harness (`measure27.sh`), whose surviving copy shows a command line identical to sweep.sh's gemv leg, and whose surviving output corroborates 13 of the 34 published values with raw `[roi] ... nrows=2` lines; a further 8 are corroborated only inside session transcripts, and 13 (K=51 baseline plus the pristine/baseline/prefetch legs of K=52-55) have no surviving nrows evidence anywhere - which is precisely the +repack and +prefetch ladder the 2.24x and 1.60x headline stages rest on. I found no sign the comparison is rigged: all measurement binaries predate 2026-08-24 and were reused unchanged by the Aug-30/31 prefill sweep, the engine and guest-RAM settings match, and the "prefill is 3.2x cheaper per token" mechanism is exactly what the source does.

result.summary: On fairness the comparison holds up well and is, if anything, conservative: all four variants share one cmake/compile line (-O3, `-march=rv64gv_zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt_zicbop_zihintpause`; only `d4` appends `_xandesvdot`), the "before" is the real vectorized upstream kernel (`ggml_vec_dot_q1_0_q8_0_vl256`, quants.c:563-577) and not a scalar straw man, all 44 sweep binaries are distinct by md5sum, all 48 27B legs report `nrows=4`, and Andes-toolchain disassembly shows a clean single-variable ladder (pristine 0 kernel `prefetch.r`, prefetch 2 per gemv/gemm entry, d4 the same prefetch plus 32 `nds.vd4dots` inside each kernel). The optimized side actually carries a handicap the doc explains but never scores: with `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF` the repack path's activation quantizer is the pure-scalar `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic` (repack.cpp:51) while pristine gets the RVV `quantize_row_q8_0`, so the ~490K-cycle `F` is charged only to the "after" and the published prefill speedups are lower bounds. Reproducibility is where this document is weak: the free end-to-end correctness check the client asked for is impossible - the ROI marker halts every run, so all 104 logs end at the `[andesim] N cycles` line with zero generated tokens, and every one of the 76 legs that reached the sampler printed a different random seed (no `-s` in sweep.sh), so no output comparison exists and none would have been meaningful; no correctness evidence of any kind is recorded for the 27B model anywhere in the repo, even though verify.sh's own header says the d4 prefill path is "not guaranteed bit-for-bit". Two further reproduction blockers: the entire 27B decode column (2.24x/1.60x/3.54x/12.64x, 12.20x, 12.53x, 12.17x, and all 12 per-node decode figures) has no raw logs on disk - there is no `sweep-gemv-27b/` and `profiling_gemv_27b.md` has no Reproducing section - and the doc's own claim "Regenerate any table with `MODEL=27b NODES=... bash sweep.sh --md`" is false: I ran both documented commands and layer 7 comes back as 4 rows at 15.02x, never the published 7 rows at 17.65x, and the tool emits no LAYER row at all.

The 28 gemv logs stop even earlier (the ROI fires in the model-init warmup pass, line 9, before system_info prints). So there is no text to compare across pristine/baseline/prefetch/d4 at any node index, on either model. Worse, the repo contains no recorded correctness evidence for the 27B model at all: verify.sh exists and does exactly the right check (--mode fast, --temp 0 greedy, text equality), q1_0_reproduce.md:89 documents `MODEL=27b bash verify.sh`, but no saved output of it exists anywhere (grep -rl 'output is identical to' finds only the runbook's own example), and opt_roadmap.md:565-566 records end-to-end text equality for Bonsai-4B only. PREFILL floats differ at the ULP level by construction" - which is precisely the path this document measures.
findings.impact: Changes no cycle number. But every headline in the document (20.67x, 18.15x, 20.60x, 17.65x) rests on kernels whose 27B output has never been shown to match upstream, on the one path the authors themselves flag as not bit-exact. findings.fix: Run `MODEL=27b bash verify.sh` once (fast mode, minutes, no RTL leg), paste its three lines and the two PASS lines into a new "Correctness" subsection of the Reproducing section, and state the acceptance bar (equal greedy text, not bit-equality) explicitly.

findings.fix: Add `-s 1 --temp 0` to the andesim invocation at sweep.sh:109-110, so future sweeps carry a greedy, seed-pinned continuation in every log and the sweep doubles as its own output-equivalence check.

findings.title: The optimized side pays a scalar activation quantizer that the baseline does not - the published prefill speedups are lower bounds, and the document never says so

The asymmetry runs in the conservative direction: it inflates the numerator of nothing and inflates the denominator of every optimized cell. The document explains the mechanism thoroughly and honestly but frames it only as "why prefill loses its edge on small tensors"; it never draws the conclusion that the reported speedups are therefore understated, nor bounds by how much.

findings.title: sweep.sh's own header misidentifies what selects the gemm vs gemv path, which can silently measure the wrong kernel
findings.claim_in_doc: The document's Reproducing section (lines 244-257) hands the reader sweep.sh, whose header (sweep.sh:16-23) states: "MODE picks the ggml path by picking the prompt, which is the ONLY thing that decides it".
findings.what_i_checked: sweep.sh:70-74 (gemm sets both PROMPT and `--no-warmup`; gemv sets only PROMPT); the line ordering in the gemv logs.
findings.finding: The prompt is not what decides it. In every sweep-gemv log the `[roi]` line appears at line 9 - before `threadpool init`, before `system_info`, and with no `sampler seed` line anywhere in the file - so the decode measurement lands in llama.cpp's model-init warmup forward pass (2 tokens), which runs regardless of the prompt. The deciding switch is `--no-warmup`: with warmup enabled, the warmup pass reaches node K first and the run is measured at nrows=2 no matter what prompt is supplied. A reader who trusts the comment and changes only the prompt gets the other kernel. In this sweep no harm was done - sweep.sh:136 catches it as BAD-NROWS and all 104 legs carry the right nrows - but the guidance is wrong.
findings.impact: No published number is affected. It is a trap for the next person reproducing this, in a script whose own header warns that "the wrong prompt measures the OTHER kernel and still prints a perfectly plausible cycle count".

result.summary: The salvaged auditor's claim is VERIFIED and the impact is BENIGN. bin-d4-k59 is provably a different build from the other eleven d4 binaries (.text +212 B, .rodata +128 B, 2 extra symbols, mtime 2026-08-07 07:47 vs 08-19/08-24 for the rest, and a `-DQ1_D4=1` that the others get as a target-level define); it alone carries the `ggml_hvm_alloc` weights-in-HVM redirect from commit 510479ad8, which lives only on branch backup-q1_0-rvv-opt-full. But it cannot have flattered anything: of 14,817 functions exactly ONE differs semantically (`ggml_backend_cpu_repack_buffer_set_tensor`, 44 -> 104 instructions, model-load only, outside the ROI); both vd4dot kernels are instruction-for-instruction identical to bin-d4-k58's (415/425 insns, 32 `nds.vd4dots` each); and the HVM path is inert three ways over (no `-DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME`, andesim's `runtime/linux/stack.h:16` "envp is always empty" so `getenv("GGML_Q1_HVM")` is NULL, and no `[q1-hvm]` line in any of the 48 logs). The other 47 binaries are perfectly consistent within their variants (identical .text/.rodata sizes, symbol counts, symbol-name digests), every log postdates its binary, all 48 logs share identical run parameters, and the shared activation quantizer is instruction-identical between the prefetch and d4 builds so the prefetch->vd4dots delta is not an `-march` windfall. findings.title: bin-d4-k59 is provably a different build, but the difference is inert and no published figure is suspect
findings.claim_in_doc: "Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one MUL_MAT node; nothing here is inferred except layer 7's three `ffn_*` rows" and the variant table row "| `d4` | `+ GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` | + `nds.vd4dots.vv` |".
findings.what_i_checked: Sizes, mtimes, .comment, readelf -S section table, nm symbol sets and symbol-name digests, per-function mnemonic fingerprints (all 14,817 functions), objdump of both vd4dot kernels, CMakeCache/compile_commands flag diffs, and log-side evidence for all 48 binaries.
findings.finding: bin-d4-k59 is the sole outlier among 48 binaries: 10,352,672 B (others 10,352,568), .text +212 B, .rodata +128 B, 2 extra symbols, built 2026-08-07 07:47 while the rest of the d4 set was built 08-19/08-24. It was configured before build.sh existed (commit 5d01611f1, 08-07 15:46) and carries `-DQ1_D4=1` in the global CMAKE_*_FLAGS rather than as the GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT target define. The extra code is the `ggml_hvm_alloc` weights-in-HVM redirect from commit 510479ad8, which is reachable only from branch backup-q1_0-rvv-opt-full, not from q1_0-rvv-opt. HOWEVER: exactly one function differs semantically (`ggml_backend_cpu_repack_buffer_set_tensor`, 44 -> 104 instructions), it runs at model load outside the ROI bracket, and the redirect provably never fired (no -DGGML_Q1_HVM_NAME; andesim runtime/linux/stack.h:16 gives the guest an empty envp so getenv returns NULL; no `[q1-hvm]` line in any log). Both vd4dot kernels are instruction-for-instruction identical to bin-d4-k58's, 32 nds.vd4dots each. The other 40 differing functions are addi-family objdump aliases flipped by the address shift.
findings.impact: The number it produced is attn_output d4 = 6,337,136 (layer-7 row, 18.90x). It is NOT an outlier: against same-shape ssm_out (6144x5120) it is 2.52% cheaper at d4 while its own untainted pristine leg is 2.33% cheaper at upstream and its prefetch leg 1.13% cheaper -- i.e. K=59 is simply a slightly cheaper node. Under the maximally hostile assumption that the whole d4 edge is an artifact, forcing attn_output's d4 to ssm_out's prefetch->d4 ratio gives 6,427,398 (+1.42%): attn_output 18.90x -> 18.63x, layer-7 4-measured geomean 15.02x -> 14.97x, and the 10-node headline 18.15x -> 18.13x. No headline moves. Verdict: the claim is verified, the difference is benign.
findings.fix: Rebuild bin-d4-k59 from branch HEAD with `ROI_K=59 bash build.sh d4` and re-run that one leg (~1 h at 6.3M cycles), then state in the doc that all 48 binaries come from one tree. If a re-run is not affordable, add a footnote to the attn_output row recording that its d4 leg came from a 2026-08-07 tree that additionally contained the (inactive) HVM redirect, with the bounded 1.4% sensitivity above.

findings.title: None of the 48 binaries can be rebuilt from branch HEAD, and the shipped codegen gate refuses to run on any of their build trees
findings.claim_in_doc: The Setup variant table "| `d4` | `+ GGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON` | + `nds.vd4dots.vv` |" plus the Reproducing section, which implies the checked-in tree produces these binaries.
findings.what_i_checked: Compared the kernel symbol names in all 12 d4 binaries against the current source; read commit f480bccff and its full diff; read check-vd4dots.sh's gate conditions and KERNELS list.
findings.finding: Every measured d4 binary contains `_ZL19q1_gemv_64d4_vl1024...` / `_ZL19q1_gemm_64d4_vl1024...` and was compiled with `-DQ1_D4=1`. Commit f480bccff (2026-08-27, after the 08-19/08-24 builds) renamed those to `q1_gemv_64_vd4dot_vl1024` / `q1_gemm_64_vd4dot_vl1024` and changed the macro to `Q1_VD4DOT`. check-vd4dots.sh hard-exits with "$BUILD is not a Q1_VD4DOT build" on any of these trees (it greps the recorded compile line for `-DQ1_VD4DOT=1`) and its KERNELS list names symbols none of these binaries contains. So the project's own gate against the "gemm silently ran generic" failure -- the one the script says "was real" for the whole F8 sweep -- cannot be run against the artifacts that produced these numbers.
findings.impact: No number changes: I verified the rename commit is identifiers, whitespace and comments only, and I independently confirmed by disassembly that both kernels really carry 32 nds.vd4dots in every d4 binary. But the doc's chain of custody from source to figure is broken in the one place a gate was built to protect, and a rebuild from HEAD yields a binary that is not the one on disk.
findings.fix: Add a line to Setup recording the commit each binary set was built from (e.g. "binaries predate f480bccff; kernels are named q1_gem[vm]_64d4_vl1024 and gated on Q1_D4"), and make check-vd4dots.sh accept either macro/name spelling so it can be pointed at the archived b-d4* trees.

findings.title: Every log reports `RVV_VLEN = 128` while Setup claims VLEN 1024, with no note reconciling them
findings.claim_in_doc: "| Engine | `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3` -- VLEN 1024, 1 hart, 32 KB L1D, no L2, 2 MB L3 |"
findings.what_i_checked: The system_info line in all 48 sweep-gemm-27b logs; the source of that string (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.cpp:602); the runtime VLEN dispatch in arch/riscv/repack.cpp:2163-2166 and 2186-2189.
findings.finding: All 48 logs print `RVV_VLEN = 128`. That field is the compile-time `__riscv_v_min_vlen` implied by `-march=rv64gv`, not the engine's VLEN; the kernels dispatch at runtime on `__riscv_vlenb() >= 128` bytes. Nothing in the document or the logs says so.
findings.impact: No number changes -- I proved the engine is VLEN>=1024 indirectly, since the 2.5x prefetch-to-d4 separation only exists on the vlenb>=128 branch (below it the d4 build falls through to the same q1_gemv_64x1_vl512 as prefetch and the two columns would coincide). But a third-party auditor reading the primary evidence sees `RVV_VLEN = 128` in every single log and has no way to reconcile it with the headline Setup row without disassembling the dispatch.
findings.fix: One line under Setup: "the `RVV_VLEN = 128` in the logs is ggml's compile-time `__riscv_v_min_vlen` from -march=rv64gv; the kernels select the vl1024 path at runtime on `__riscv_vlenb() >= 128` (arch/riscv/repack.cpp:2163), which is what the engine reports."
